articles.headline: Pistons predicted to trade for ex-Heat $120M sniper with Finals experience to address major need
keyFacts: The Milwaukee Bucks traded Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Miami Heat for Tyler Herro and multiple draft picks, according to ESPN sources.
CBS Sports analyst Sam Quinn predicted that Tyler Herro could eventually be traded from the Bucks to the Detroit Pistons.
Quinn stated that Herro could provide the Pistons with a reliable perimeter shooter and an additional scoring option to strengthen their championship hopes.
body: This offseason marked a major turning point for the Milwaukee Bucks, as the franchise officially changed course and reshaped its future. Milwaukee is now entering a rebuild, hoping that investing in young talent will pay off in the long run.
The Bucks had to start somewhere, and that meant trading franchise superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat.

“The Milwaukee Bucks are trading franchise icon Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Miami Heat for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks (including No. 13 in Tuesday's NBA draft), one pick swap and one second-round pick, sources told ESPN. The Heat are sending to Milwaukee unprotected first-rounders in 2031 and 2033 along with No. 13, a pick swap in 2030 and a 2033 second-rounder, according to sources," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.
Tyler Herro is arguably the most notable player headed to Milwaukee in the deal. However, CBS Sports' Sam Quinn believes Herro could eventually be traded to the Detroit Pistons.

“Detroit was the rumored destination in the offseason, and it was a sensible one. The Pistons can cover for him defensively better than most suitors. They need another high-end shot-creator, but can't pay max money for one with Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson now extended,” Quinn wrote.
Herro could provide exactly what the Pistons have been missing over the past year. The veteran guard would give Detroit another reliable perimeter shooter and an additional scoring option.

“Most notably, the Pistons are even snagging wins when they shoot poorly from beyond the arc. In an era of basketball where consistency from three-point range is preached as paramount, the Detroit Pistons are winning in their own way. Their tough defense and efficiency inside the paint has defined their identity this season," SI's Aidan Chacon wrote.

A potential trade could benefit both sides. The Bucks would have another opportunity to get younger and continue building for the future, while the Pistons could add an established scorer to strengthen their championship hopes. With Detroit looking to take the next step, Herro could be an appealing target.

Herro is entering the final year of his $120 million deal, making a potential trade a gamble for Detroit if he is only a short-term addition. However, if the Pistons believe he can help them win a championship, the risk could be worth taking.

articles.headline: Brandeis, Smithson Valley prevail in volleyball playoff doubleheader
keyFacts: Brandeis and Smithson Valley won volleyball playoff matches in a doubleheader on Thursday at Littleton Gym.
Brandeis defeated Pieper in three sets and will next face Dripping Springs in the second round.
Smithson Valley defeated Alamo Heights in four sets and will next face Laredo Nixon.
body: Brandeis players celebrates after beating Pieper during a 28-6A bi-district playoff game on Thursday, October 29, 2026 at Littleton Gym in San Antonio. (Charlie Blalock/For the Express-News)
Riding the momentum that carried them to district championships, Brandeis and Smithson Valley recorded playoff victories in a doubleheader held Thursday at Littleton Gym.
Junior Cecily Alva had 15 kills and freshman Addison Wells had 40 assists to lead Brandeis to a 25-17, 25-18, 26-24 victory against Pieper in a Class 6A Division II first-round playoff.
Meanwhile, freshman Victoria Jaster had 22 kills, and senior Emma Feomaia had 41 assists for Smithson Valley in a 25-20, 25-20, 23-25, 25-12 win against Alamo Heights in a 5A Division I playoff.

Brandeis climbed out of a third-set hole to secure the sweep. Junior Olivia Munoz added 14 kills and junior Addison Rodgers had 12 for the Broncos, who improved to 30-13 and next face Dripping Springs - a five-set winner over Round Rock Stony Point Thursday - in the second round.

Brandeis trailed 17-11 in the third set before mounting its comeback. Pieper (27-16) nearly stretched it to a fourth set after taking a 23-18 lead. The Broncos responded with a 6-0 run to reach match point at 24-23. Alva had two kills and Araceli had an ace during that stretch.
After Pieper erased one match point, the Broncos secured it by forcing a hitting error on the second match point.

"We're the kind of team that doesn't give up," Munoz said. "We've had games where we've been down further than those points and we came back and won."

In the first set, Brandeis led 14-13 before a lengthy serving run from Munoz got things going for the Broncos, who extended their lead to 23-13. Munoz had three aces and Rodgers had two kills and a block during that sequence that put the first set out of reach for Pieper.

"I think serving to a tough team like that is very important," Munoz said. "It definitely kept the momentum of our team, and I feel that allowed us to win. We're a team that has grit and we really dig deep and we want to win at the end of the day."
After dropping the first point, Brandeis never trailed in the second set. The Broncos held the lead at 8-2, 19-15 and 23-16 before locking it up with a block by Wells.

Brandeis had defeated Pieper twice before entering Thursday's match. The Broncos outlasted the Warriors in four sets in a non-district match on Aug. 25. Two days later, Brandeis prevailed in two sets in a tournament contest.
After starting 1-2 in District 28-6A, the Broncos won 11 in a row to earn a co-championship with Reagan. They showed that type of determination to win the third set.

"That definitely gave us a lot of momentum coming into playoffs, especially that Reagan game mid-district season. It gave us that mindset that we played the hardest team in our district and beat them in three. We can keep going and we have so much more potential to keep building off of."
Smithson Valley entered the postseason with an undefeated run (14-0) in winning the District 25-5A title.

"That gave us a bunch of confidence, but not so much that we're going to be overconfident," Feomaia said. "It definitely puts some experience under our belt when we go into playoffs."
The Rangers led for most of the third set before a late rush allowed Alamo Heights (29-14) to take it. Smithson Valley was up 22-18 before the Mules went on 7-1 run that sealed it.
Smithson Valley rebounded with a strong finish by Jaster, whose 22nd kill capped a 6-0 run that secured the match.
"Everybody in the gym knows she's a big hitter," Feomaia said. "Whenever we're in trouble, I know who to go to, and that's Tori."
Smithson Valley next faces Laredo Nixon, which defeated Highlands on Thursday.

articles.headline: Where to watch the Brewers parade: Start time, TV channels, live streams for Milwaukee World Series celebration
keyFacts: The Milwaukee Brewers won the World Series for the first time in franchise history.
A championship parade and rally are scheduled to take place in downtown Milwaukee on Friday at 10 a.m. local time.
Fans can watch the event nationally on MLB Network or via live streams on Fubo.
body: A party decades in the making is set to take over Milwaukee on Friday.

After dominating all comers throughout the regular season and playoffs, the Brewers are World Series champions for the first time. Considering that franchise moved to Milwaukee in 1970 and the city's only previous triumph was the Braves' Fall Classic win over the Yankees in 1957, Friday is shaping up to be an all-time party.

An Associated Press story detailing the welcome the champion Braves got upon returning home from New York 69 years ago describes about 250,000 people crowding into an area two blocks wide and two miles long down Wisconsin Avenue. That's in addition to some 20,000 who reportedly greeted the team at the airport at 7:30 p.m. before they set out on a somewhat impromptu parade of 30 convertibles in 47-degree temperatures with a strong wind off the lake. Photos from that evening show an endless sea of people that forced police to clear a path so the team's vehicles could get through.

Friday's event will be much more organized, with a parade followed by a rally, but the crowd numbers figure to dwarf that long-ago celebration. It will be a day to remember for Milwaukee and Brewers fans everywhere. Here's when and where to watch, no matter where you are.
Brewers World Series parade start time
- Date: Friday, Oct. 30
- Time: 10 a.m. CT | 11 a.m. ET

The Brewers' World Series championship parade is set to begin Friday at 10 a.m. local time, or 11 a.m. ET. The procession will travel through downtown Milwaukee on the way to Henry Maier Festival Park, where a celebration rally will follow. See the full parade route below.
Where to watch the Brewers World Series parade
- TV channels: MLB Network (national)
- Live streams: Fubo
Fans around the country can tune in to coverage of the Brewers parade and rally on MLB Network, which can be streamed with Fubo.

Fubo offers a free trial for new subscribers, so you can try the service before you buy. Stream ESPN, ABC, CBS, Fox, NBC and 100+ top channels of live TV and sports without cable. (Participating plans only. Taxes and fees may apply.)
Brewers World Series parade route
The parade is set to begin at 4th St. and Wisconsin Ave. in downtown Milwaukee, heading east toward the river.

The procession will turn north on Jefferson at the Pfister Hotel — renowned in MLB circles for purportedly being haunted — then travel a block before going east on Mason St., then turning south on Jackson St. a block later. The route crosses under I-794 and eventually to Chicago St. for another turn east before arriving at Henry Maier Festival Park.

articles.headline: Crypto giant Binance hit by hack suspected to be largest in history
keyFacts: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said $6.3bn of digital assets were impacted by a suspected hack involving a compromised engineer laptop.
Two analytics firms attributed the incident to North Korean hacking unit TraderTraitor, though Binance did not directly respond to those links.
Binance said about half of the assets have been frozen with help from other platforms and that it will cover all losses.
body: - Published
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what has been described as the "largest hack in history".
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses".
Early checks show the incident may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.
Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added.
Chainalysis, another crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC queries about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."

The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
"Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said.
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they have frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Circle chief executive Jeremy Allaire said his firm is "closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance" and that his company has frozen more than $800m in assets linked to the incident.
Circle is the issuer and co-creator of the USDC, one of the world's largest US dollar-backed cryptocurrencies.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said his firm has frozen around $1.6bn "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."
"Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority," said Ardoino, whose company issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under custody.
Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply.

articles.headline: Venezuela’s Machado lauds Trump for ‘freedom’, urges 2027 elections
keyFacts: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned from exile and thanked the Trump administration for abducting President Nicolas Maduro.
Former Vice President Delcy Rodriguez currently leads Venezuela, while Machado stated she returned to Caracas to mobilize society.
Machado urged holding presidential elections in 2027, while Rodriguez assured elections would happen without specifying a date.
body: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado has thanked US President Donald Trump’s administration for opening the “floodgate to freedom” by abducting President Nicolas Maduro in January.
The Nobel Peace Prize laureate on Thursday also called for elections to be held in Venezuela next year, in her first public remarks since returning from more than 10 months in exile.

“Thanks to their vision, their courage, and their action on January 3, the floodgate to freedom has been opened,” Machado told a news conference in Caracas, naming Trump, his administration and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Rubio “has set out a sequence of events aimed at moving toward a democratic transition that makes clear the holding of presidential elections in 2027”, she said.
Machado has praised Trump before, presenting the president with her Nobel medal – a prize he feverishly coveted for himself in 2025.

A longtime activist, Machado fled Venezuela for Oslo in December to accept the Nobel Peace Prize. On Thursday, she said she had come home to “mobilise society”. US special forces veterans with an organisation called Grey Bull Rescue helped Machado escape by boat after she spent a year in hiding from Maduro’s regime.
Since Maduro’s abduction in January, the country has been ruled by his former Vice President Delcy Rodriguez.
Machado was greeted by cheering supporters as she travelled in her motorcade after she returned to Venezuela on Sunday. Rodriguez voiced distaste for the fanfare.
“The show could have been avoided – the airports are right here,” she said on state television.
When asked about a possible meeting with Rodriguez, the opposition leader said she had not received any message from her or from Washington.
Shortly before Machado’s statements on Thursday, Rodriguez assured the nation that elections would be held in Venezuela “with the world as witness” but did not specify a date.
Her return comes just weeks after a controversial US oil deal that will see Venezuela hand over 20 percent of its vast oil reserves.
“This agreement does not reflect the levels of transparency that Venezuelan society wants,” Machado said, criticising the deal.

articles.headline: Germany news: Friedrich Merz calls for global free trade alliance during Asia trip
keyFacts: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for a global free trade network based on international rules during a conference in South Korea.
Merz stated that escalating competition between the United States and China is fundamentally changing the rules of the global economy.
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is scheduled to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a visit to China.
body: What you need to know
- Chancellor Friedrich Merz is ending his multi-day trip to Asia
- President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is set to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping
Here are the leading headlines from Germany on Friday, October 30:
Merz pushes for new free trade network
Chancellor Merz has again called for a global network of countries with a commitment to free trade based on international rules.

"Competition between the US and China is ramping up. Tariffs, technological decoupling strategies and a tough race for critical raw materials and new technologies are fundamentally changing the rules of our global economy," Merz said. "These conflicts and systemic shifts in power pattern concern us all. They particularly concern economically aspiring partners in the Indo-Pacific, as well as in Germany and in Europe."
His comments came while in South Korea on the final day of his four-day trip to Asia. He was speaking at the Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business in Seoul.
"We are resolutely joining forces against unilateralism, autocratic power politics and violations of international law," he said.

"When supply chains become political pawns, when access to key technologies is obstructed or when efforts to secure raw materials resemble displays of power rather than fair partnerships, this jeopardizes growth, prosperity and ultimately the security of entire regions," Merz added.
The chancellor had made a similar call in Singapore and Japan.
"German companies are using Korea as a central hub to expand their presence in the Asia-Pacific region," South Korean Prime Minister Han Seong Sook said at Thursday's conference.

articles.headline: Packers' Christian Watson returns against Panthers after chest injury, hospital visit
keyFacts: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson returned to the game in the third quarter after being transported to a hospital for precautionary tests following a first-half chest injury.
Medical staff sent Watson to the hospital after he spat up blood during a collision with Carolina Panthers cornerback Will Lee III, but tests ultimately ruled out internal bleeding.
Watson finished the contest with additional padding around his ribs, adding receptions in the fourth quarter to help the Packers secure the victory.
body: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson returned to the Week 8 "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Carolina Panthers in the third quarter after departing in the first half with a chest injury. Watson was transported to a hospital near Lambeau Field for precautionary tests and returned to the stadium shortly after halftime. The team initially deemed him questionable to play, and upon his clearance, he reentered the contest.

Watson arrived back at Lambeau Field in an ambulance and ran into the locker room, where he spent about three minutes preparing for a return to action. He emerged onto the sideline with additional padding around his ribs and pointed to the lower right side of his chest when teammates inquired about the injury, according to Prime Video's Kaylee Hartung.

"It was tough," Watson said to Hartung during the postgame show. "I never wanted to go. I was hoping they would let me off. I said I was feeling better once I kind of caught my breath. They said there was a couple of signs that made them have to take me over there. It is what it is. I was just praying that it was good enough to where I could come back out here. Thankfully it was, and I was able to get back out. I'm trying to be on the football field. That's first and foremost for me."

Watson said that he spit up blood upon sustaining the injury, which was a trigger for the Packers' medical staff to take him to the hospital. Tests ruled out internal bleeding, which opened the door for him to play. He said that he monitored the game from his hospital room and watched the play-by-play feed while waiting for the results of his tests.

The injury occurred on the biggest play of the first half: A 53-yard reception that set up the Packers' second touchdown of the night. Watson collided with Panthers cornerback Will Lee III, who was also injured on the play. Carolina ruled Lee doubtful to return with a hamstring injury.

Watson was in the midst of a massive performance when he departed from the contest. He led all receivers in the first half with six catches for 100 yards. His ability to separate from the maligned Panthers defense was instrumental in quarterback Jordan Love completing 17 of his first 20 passes on the night.

The Packers dialed up a pass in Watson's direction on his first play back from the hospital, and while he did not come up with the catch, he did add a pair of receptions in the fourth quarter. The second of those two grabs nearly iced the game, as it converted a third down and allowed the Packers to drain valuable time off the clock and limit the Panthers to mere seconds on their final possession.

Matthew Golden stepped up in Watson's absence as the No. 1 option in Green Bay's receiving unit. He caught a touchdown pass on the Packers' first possession without Watson and redeemed himself for dropping a would-be scoring pass on the previous play. Tucker Kraft also played an increased role downfield and was responsible for the Packers' first touchdown on Thursday.

Injuries, unfortunately, have been a defining element of Watson's NFL career. He has an extensive history that includes a separate chest injury, three hamstring strains, an ankle sprain, three knee bruises and an ACL tear. He also sustained a concussion during his rookie season in 2022. In all, Watson has missed 20 games and is yet to play a full season across five years in the league.

articles.headline: 10 Essential Fantasy Books You Need to Read at Least Once in Your Life
keyFacts: Polygon published a list of ten essential fantasy books that explore humanity through extraordinary worlds and masterworks.
The featured books include foundational and diverse titles such as The Neverending Story, The Witcher collection, and The Lord of the Rings.
The article highlights how these novels reshape storytelling, challenge assumptions, and influence generations of fantasy literature.
body: Fantasy has always offered a way to step beyond the boundaries of reality, inviting readers into worlds where the impossible becomes part of everyday life. The genre stretches back to ancient folklore, epic poetry, and fairy tales, existing long before the modern fantasy novel took shape, in which sorcery and magical worlds abound. From the mythological journeys of Homer to the dreamlike stories of George MacDonald, imaginative literature has continually found new ways to explore humanity through the extraordinary.

Over time, foundational authors like J.R.R. Tolkien, Ursula K. Le Guin, and Terry Pratchett expanded the boundaries of the genre, crafting timeless epics that redefined what speculative fiction could even look like. Works like The Once and Future King, The Fifth Season, and Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell showcase the immense thematic range and literary ambition of modern fantasy.

But what makes a great fantasy novel essential? It isn't merely world-building or magic systems; it’s the rare ability to shatter our assumptions about storytelling, reshape the genre in its image, and echo across generations. The following 10 masterworks represent the pinnacle of fantasy literature, featuring a diverse range of books every reader should experience at least once before they die.
10 The Neverending Story (1979) by Michael Ende

The Neverending Story is a reminder that the greatest fantasy adventures often begin with a simple act of curiosity, which ironically starts with a book in this case. When Bastian Balthazar Bux comes upon a mysterious novel, he becomes immersed in Fantastica, a world threatened by a dangerous and malignant force known as the Nothing. As the boundary between spectator and hero begins to dissolve, Bastian realizes that saving this fragile realm depends entirely on his own capacity to dream.

Michael Ende understood that imagination can be both a refuge and a responsibility, turning a simple escape from reality into something deeply personal. The Neverending Story blurs the boundaries between reader and story in ways few fantasy novels manage, exploring the dangers of losing oneself in a world of your own making. Beneath its colorful creatures and extraordinary landscapes lies a thoughtful meditation on the stories we tell ourselves and how they can shape our identity, capturing the transformative power of reading that few books have mustered since.
9 The Lies of Locke Lamora (2006) by Scott Lynch

Fantasy doesn't always need ancient prophecies, world-ending wars, or chosen-one heroes destined to save the day. Sometimes, all it needs is a clever thief with an elaborate scheme and absolutely no intention of playing by the rules. That’s how Scott Lynch's The Lies of Locke Lamora recontextualizes the classic approach to fantasy. The story follows the Gentleman Bastards, a band of con artists who prey on the wealthy citizens of Camorr, a city whose Venetian-inspired streets are filled with political intrigue and criminal enterprise. Locke himself is a master manipulator, but his elaborate deceptions become increasingly dangerous when a mysterious figure threatens to upend everything he has built.

Lynch does a fantastic job of balancing razor-sharp dialogue and intricate plotting with a world that feels both dangerous and endlessly entertaining. For readers who prefer their fantasy with a criminal touch, elaborate cons, and characters who survive through wit rather than brute strength, The Lies of Locke Lamora is essential reading.
8 The Last Unicorn (1968) by Peter S. Beagle

There is a quiet heartbreak at the core of The Last Unicorn, a novel that understands a creature's magic is inseparable from the tragedy of its potential loss. Peter S. Beagle follows a unicorn who discovers she may be the last of her kind and sets out to find the others, embarking on a journey filled with eccentric companions and dangerous magic, the hallmarks of a great fantasy tale. Her search eventually drives her toward the malevolent King Haggard and the fearsome Red Bull, where uncovering the truth about her species requires risking her immortality.

What makes the novel so enduring is Beagle's willingness to look beyond the familiar comforts of fairy tales. His prose is playful and poetic, but there's a melancholy running beneath the adventure that gives every encounter monumental weight. It’s why The Last Unicorn feels like a story about the painful passage of time. It's proof that fantasy can be enchanting without sacrificing the emotional complexity that makes its stories linger long after the final page.
7 The Last Wish (1993) by Andrzej Sapkowski

Before Geralt of Rivia became a household name through video games and television, Andrzej Sapkowski introduced readers to a monster hunter whose greatest challenge isn't always the monstrous creatures he encounters. First published in 1993, The Last Wish collects interconnected stories that establish the foundations of The Witcher, drawing from European folklore while gleefully dismantling the conventions of traditional fairy tales. Here, familiar legends take on unexpected detours, princesses mutate into gory monsters, and the distinction between humanity and monstrosity is considerably harder to establish.

Geralt's profession demands that he navigate these moral ambiguities, often discovering that the people paying him are far more dangerous and ugly than the beasts he has been hired to kill. Sapkowski's sharp dialogue and dark humor give the collection a personality all its own. For anyone interested in fantasy that questions its own mythology, The Last Wish remains an excellent starting point. And with The Witcher 4 just around the corner, now is the perfect time to dive into Sapkowski's literary world.
6 Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World (1985) by Haruki Murakami

There aren’t many fantasy novels that feel quite as disorienting as Haruki Murakami's Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World. Like many of Murakami’s stories, it’s one that seems determined to keep its readers guessing about the nature of reality itself. Alternating between two seemingly unrelated worlds, Hard-Boiled Wonderland juxtaposes a futuristic Tokyo filled with secretive organizations against a strange, walled town where a man must surrender his shadow to read dreams. As these narratives gradually converge, Murakami inevitably showcases the fragile boundaries that separate identity from imagination, charting how the protagonist’s physical self in Tokyo edges toward irreversible brain death.

Murakami’s fusion of cybernetic noir, surrealism, and dreamlike fantasy makes Hard-Boiled Wonderland an unorthodox choice for an essential fantasy list, but that’s exactly why it belongs. Rather than providing easy answers, the novel asks readers to surrender to its mysteries and ponder what remains of identity when memory is stripped away. It’s a thoughtful meditation on solitude, told through a distinct Japanese perspective that’s fitting for every fan of fantasy literature.
5 A Wizard of Earthsea (1968) by Ursula K. Le Guin

Magic has rarely felt as meaningful as it does in Ursula K. Le Guin's A Wizard of Earthsea, the foundational masterpiece that launched her iconic Earthsea Cycle. The novel follows Ged, a gifted young wizard whose pride leads him to unleash a terrible shadow upon the world, forcing him to confront the consequences of his own hubris. Ged’s journey turns into a desperate cat-and-mouse quest that takes him across a vast archipelago of isolated islands, ancient dragon-lords, and forgotten traditions as he pursues — and is pursued by — the very shadow he unleashed.

All the while, Le Guin spends time expertly detailing the ecology of magic itself, a system governed by the power of "true names" and the delicate balance of the cosmos. Ged's journey is not about conquering an external villain, but accepting his own darkness, setting a template for coming-of-age fantasy that is both mythic and deeply intimate. Its philosophical wisdom makes it an indispensable cornerstone of the genre.
4 The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath (1943) by H.P. Lovecraft

If fantasy is the art of imagining worlds beyond our own, few writers ventured into stranger territory than H. P. Lovecraft. Although better known for cosmic horror, Lovecraft’s The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath makes a compelling case for itself as one of the most singular achievements in surreal fantasy. Published posthumously in 1943, the tale follows Randolph Carter as he journeys through the Dreamlands in search of a magnificent city he has glimpsed in his dreams. Along the way, Carter encounters bizarre civilizations, terrifying creatures, and landscapes that seem to obey a logic entirely their own.

Lovecraft's fascination with cosmic horror is evident throughout, yet this sprawling novella is also a remarkable exercise in imaginative worldbuilding, drawing together elements of mythology, dark fantasy, and surreal adventure. Its dreamlike narrative can be disorienting, but that's part of its appeal. Rather than offering a familiar quest with clearly defined rules and antagonists, Lovecraft creates a universe that feels ancient, unknowable, and indifferent to human understanding. It's an essential detour into fantasy's darker corners put forth by one of horror literature’s most acclaimed visionaries.
3 Weaveworld (1987) by Clive Barker

Clive Barker has always understood that the most extraordinary fantasy worlds can exist just beyond the edges of everyday life. In Weaveworld, that simple idea takes shape in the Fugue, a wonderfully bizarre realm home to the magical Seerkind, woven into the fabric of an ordinary Persian carpet. When its hidden inhabitants face destruction from a ruthless ancient enemy, the fate of their world becomes entangled with two unsuspecting humans thrust into a fight for survival.

Approaching fantasy with the sensibilities of a horror master, Barker infuses the story with grotesque creatures, unsettling transformations, and a brand of magic that feels as perilous as it is mesmerizing. Beneath these nightmarish textures, however, beats a genuine devotion to the transformative power of imagination. By daring to venture into the visceral, the sensual, and the surreal, Weaveworld stands in stark contrast to traditional sword-and-sorcery stories, proving that fantasy is often at its most magical when it refuses to play it safe.
2 Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland (1865) by Lewis Carroll

More than 160 years after its publication, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland remains one of the strangest and most influential journeys in fantasy literature. Author Lewis Carroll sends his young protagonist tumbling into a world where familiar rules have collapsed, allowing mundane conversations to spiral into absurdity and simple questions become impossible to answer. From the perpetually hurried White Rabbit to the enigmatic Cheshire Cat and the tyrannical Queen of Hearts, Wonderland is populated by characters who seem to delight in challenging Alice's understanding of the world.

Underneath his literary pen name, Carroll was Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, an Oxford mathematician and logician whose deep understanding of formal proofs directly inspired the strict mathematical puzzles and inverted reason that govern Wonderland. That’s why the nonsense works, because it’s built on strict logic. Through wordplay, mathematical riddles, and iconic set pieces like the Caucus-Race where everyone wins or a game of croquet played with live flamingos the narrative systematically dismantles adult authority and etiquette. Alice’s attempts to apply classroom lessons to a world where a baby turns into a pig or a cat leaves its grin behind show how brittle human rules can turn under a bit of scrutiny. It remains an essential cornerstone of fantasy, demonstrating that pure playfulness can double as sharp cultural satire.
1 The Lord of the Rings (1954) by J. R. R. Tolkien

Published across three volumes between 1954 and 1955, J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings stands as fantasy’s most unforgettable tale. It follows Frodo Baggins and his companions in their attempt to destroy the One Ring, an artifact whose corrupting power threatens to plunge Middle-earth into darkness. Building directly upon the quieter adventures of The Hobbit, where Bilbo Baggins first unwittingly claimed the fateful ring from Gollum, Tolkien expands a simple fairy tale into a vast mythic saga of fellowship, war, and the tragic burden of unintended heroism.

Tolkien's achievement extends far beyond its central quest. Through ancient histories, invented languages, intricate mythology, and cultures with distinct identities, he creates a world that feels as though it existed long before the reader arrived. The story's enduring power primarily comes from its overarching theme: a belief that courage can emerge from the smallest and most unlikely individuals. Battles and grand adventures might have their place, but the burden of doing what is right alongside one’s true friends defines the journey. For anyone seeking to understand modern fantasy, Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings remains the blueprint from which nearly all speculative fiction continues to draw.

articles.headline: Packers beat Panthers as Green Bay’s Christian Watson returns after mid-game hospital visit
keyFacts: Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes and Josh Jacobs scored twice as the Green Bay Packers defeated the Carolina Panthers 27-19.
Green Bay receiver Christian Watson returned from a hospital chest evaluation to finish as the game's top receiver with 113 yards.
Several members of the Milwaukee Brewers received a stadium ovation after winning the franchise's first World Series title.
body: Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes, Josh Jacobs scored twice and the Green Bay Packers withstood three turnovers to beat the Carolina Panthers 27-19 on Thursday night.

Love went 30 of 41 for 288 yards with touchdown passes to Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Jacobs plus an interception. Although he rushed for only 39 yards on 21 carries against the NFL’s lowest-ranked run defense, Jacobs scored on a four-yard catch and one-yard run for the Packers (5-3).

After trailing 27-10 in the third quarter, Carolina cut Green Bay’s lead to 27-19 on Bryce Young’s 26-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Coker on a fourth-and-three play with 5:37 remaining. Young’s ensuing two-point conversion pass was incomplete.

The Panthers (3-4) got the ball back at their own 45 before losing the ball on downs at midfield with 2:41 remaining. Carolina got one last chance from their own 20 with 22 seconds and no timeouts remaining, but Dani Dennis-Sutton’s sack essentially ended any comeback hopes.
Young went 23 of 31 for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Carolina’s Chuba Hubbard had 22 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown and seven catches for 38 yards.

Green Bay’s Christian Watson was involved in a remarkable sequence of events. He hurt his chest making a 53-yard catch in the second quarter. The Packers feared he may have sustained a serious injury, and he was taken to a local hospital. However, after being passed fit by doctors, he returned late in the third quarter, then caught a six-yard pass on the opening play of the fourth. He finished as the game’s top receiver with 113 yards on eight receptions.

“I never wanted to go [to hospital], I was hoping they’d let me off,” Watson said after the game. “They said there were a couple of signs that made them want to take me over there, so I was just praying it was good enough that I could come back out here. Luckily it was … I’m happy to be out here on a football field. There was no internal bleeding [nothing] that was raising suspicion. I cleared everything and I was able to get back out.”
Watson said he had been able to follow the game while he was in hospital. “One of the doctors had his phone out, so I was watching the play-by-play,” he said.

Carolina cornerback Will Lee hurt his hamstring while diving to make a tackle on the same play in which Watson was injured, and he was carted into the locker room. Carolina already have three other cornerbacks on injured reserve: Akayleb Evans (triceps/knee), Mike Jackson (groin) and Jaycee Horn (quadriceps).
Brewers get big welcome

There was a warm welcome for another Wisconsin team on Thursday night. Several members of the Milwaukee Brewers, including team captain Christian Yelich and Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski, received a huge ovation as they arrived Lambeau Field one night after winning the first World Series title in franchise history.

Brewers pitcher Brandon Woodruff held the Commissioner’s Trophy aloft as he emerged from the tunnel during a timeout before the second quarter. A few of the players attempted a Lambeau Leap into the crowd, with outfielder Sal Frelick having the most success.
Those Brewers players later were shown on the video board cheering as they wore cheeseheads that included the message, “2026 WS Champions.”

articles.headline: Final Israeli election results show Netanyahu falling short as his party alleges fraud
keyFacts: Benjamin Netanyahu and his bloc fell short of a 61-seat Knesset majority after winning 53 seats in finalized election results.
The opposition bloc, which won 48 seats, could form a majority government if it unites with Arab parties holding 19 seats.
All votes are counted, but the election results must be certified and submitted to President Isaac Herzog next Wednesday.
body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the right-wing Likud party fell short of gaining a 61-seat majority needed to control the Knesset as the election results were finalized.

Netanyahu’s bloc secured 53 seats, while the opposition bloc, led by former Israel Defense Forces chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot , won 48 seats and the Arab parties the remaining 19 seats. This puts Netanyahu’s party in a bind, as the opposition bloc could choose to join forces with the Arab parties to form a majority government.
The alliance would be a direct repudiation of Netanyahu, who blamed alleged foreign election interference for boosting the Arab vote in Israel’s legislative elections on Tuesday.

“The elections in the State of Israel were stolen by Arab parties that support terrorism and the elimination of the Jewish state through serious criminal offenses of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries, and the use of prohibited software to mobilize voters,” Netanyahu posted on X.

“The Likud party is transferring to the police, the Shin Bet, and the Central Elections Committee hundreds of testimonies and pieces of evidence regarding election theft in many Arab polling stations,” he wrote, naming various pieces of evidence.
Following an order by Israel’s top election official, the Shin Bet is investigating suspected Qatari and Turkish funding to boost Arab turnout at polling locations this week.

Qatar denied the “ridiculous and dangerous” allegations that it was involved in swaying Israel’s elections, and Eisenkot mocked Netanyahu’s promotion of the foreign interference allegations before an investigation got underway.
“I commend Netanyahu for finally condemning Qatari involvement in the State of Israel,” he said , referencing accusations that the prime minister’s former top aides accepted money from Qatar.

“Foreign involvement in the State of Israel is an unacceptable and gravely serious matter, especially when it involves a country that funds and supports the Hamas organization,” Eisenkot added. “This is grave when it happens in the Prime Minister’s Office and grave if it occurs in the election system.”

The opposition leader wants the Shin Bet to investigate the allegations “impartially, thoroughly, and immediately” while respecting the rights of voters. He specifically called out Netanyahu for waging an “illegitimate influence operation on the Israeli public.”
ISRAELI TOP ELECTION OFFICIAL ORDERS SHIN BET TO INVESTIGATE ALLEGATIONS OF FOREIGN INTERFERENCE WITH ARAB VOTE

Israeli President Isaac Herzog warned about demonizing Arab Israeli voters, saying “we must not tarnish an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy.”
All votes are counted, but the results need to be certified and submitted to Herzog next Wednesday.

articles.headline: Security experts warn North Korean hackers aren't just using AI in their new campaigns, but also 'post-quantum' encryption
keyFacts: Kaspersky reported that the North Korean hacking group Lazarus targeted at least three South Korean firms in a campaign active since July 2025.
Kaspersky said the group used an updated malware tool featuring ML-KEM-1024 post-quantum cryptography to secure payload delivery against future decryption.
Kaspersky advised defenders to focus on blocking the initial spear-phishing delivery vector and maintaining strong endpoint security.
body: - Kaspersky says Lazarus's Operation FlashHole, active since at least July 2025, hit at least three South Korean software, construction, and telecom equipment firms
- An updated LPEClient tool uses four ML-KEM-1024 key exchanges to protect payload delivery, a design Check Point also documented
- The post-quantum layer guards traffic against future decryption, not endpoint detection, and the most likely way in for the hackers was still phishing

North Korea's most notorious hacking group has been caught protecting its malware with the same post-quantum cryptography that governments and tech firms are still rolling out to safeguard their own data.

In its analysis of a campaign dubbed Operation FlashHole, Kaspersky's Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT) says an updated version of LPEClient, a Lazarus Group tool, now uses ML-KEM-1024, a key exchange mechanism designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers, to secure the channel it uses to download more malware.

The findings describe a campaign active since at least July 2025 that has hit at least three South Korean organizations in the software, construction, and wired communication equipment manufacturing sectors.
A fake AI-tailored résumé, a mandatory plugin, and quantum-resistant encryption

The way in was familiar: Kaspersky found a GitHub Pages site tied to a GitHub account, created in September 2025, that the attackers used for command and control. The site first showed the résumé of a supposed senior network appliance developer, likely seen by an employee of the communications equipment maker, before the attackers swapped it in January 2026for an interior design showcase that probably targeted the construction firm.

Kaspersky assesses with medium-to-high confidence that targets received spear-phishing emails linking to these sites, which loaded JavaScript from attacker-controlled domains, though it could not determine exactly what triggered the infection.

From there, the chain ran through INISAFE CrossWeb EX, financial security software South Koreans need in order to use many online banking and government websites. How it was abused is unclear, but the malware ended up running in memory with elevated privileges, spawned by a CrossWeb EX build released in 2023 after a public advisory from South Korea's KrCERT.

That is a well-trodden route; Kaspersky says Lazarus abused CrossWeb EX in 2021, 2022, and 2023, and in Operation SyncHole, disclosed in April 2025, it used Cross EX, a related program, to compromise at least six organizations, and we also reported on the group exploiting a zero-day in MagicLine4NX, another South Korean authentication tool.

Kaspersky believes the photo on the résumé site was AI-generated, citing missing EXIF metadata and an unnatural texture, and that AI most likely built the site too, given a candidate name resembling Korea's equivalent of "John Doe" and a portfolio stuffed with filler details and unrelated companies.

ojun Ryu, senior security researcher at Kaspersky GReAT, said the findings suggest Lazarus is "bringing AI into its long-established playbook," a shift Kaspersky has also seen among other Lazarus-aligned groups. That fits a broader pattern, from Kimsuky using ChatGPT to forge a South Korean military ID to North Korean IT workers using generative AI to get hired at Western firms.

The more striking change is inside LPEClient, a profiling and payload delivery tool that first appeared in 2019. The new version no longer stores its own server address; instead, it relays traffic through ClientHub, a newly discovered loader with a variant that talks to its operators via Dropbox. It profiles installed security products and the Windows patch level, now also checks whether protections such as Shadow Stack are enabled, and encrypts that report with GOST, Russia's national cipher standard.
A security-conscious hacker group?

Then comes the post-quantum part of the equation. The server sends four ML-KEM-1024 public keys, LPEClient derives four shared secrets from them, and those are combined into a single 128-byte key for Threefish, a tweakable block cipher originally built for the Skein hash function. That key decrypts the next payload, which is loaded straight into memory.

ML-KEM-1024 is the strongest of three parameter sets in NIST's FIPS 203 standard, and the one the NSA specifies for key establishment under CNSA 2.0, its algorithm suite for US national security systems. Kaspersky's report notes, with some irony, that the group seems to have "adopted more secure post-quantum cryptography faster than many legitimate security products."

Ryu said the part that "deserves closer attention" is the group's "adoption of cryptography designed to withstand future quantum threats," which Kaspersky traces back to at least September 2024. If that holds, Lazarus was using the technology within weeks of NIST finalizing its first post-quantum standards on August 13, 2024, and more than two years before this month's disclosure.

Kaspersky is not the first to spot this, either. In August 2026, Check Point Research described a module in a separate Dream Job wave against defense companies that fetched four public keys from its server and used Kyber/ML-KEM to agree on a key to download FudModule, a rootkit that exploited the since-patched Windows zero-day CVE-2026-68820. Kaspersky identifies the module as LPEClient, and the campaign received widespread coverage at the time.

No publicly known quantum computer can yet break the classical key exchanges that protect most internet traffic, so ML-KEM only gives Lazarus an edge if someone records its traffic today and decrypts it once such a machine exists- the "harvest now, decrypt later" scenario driving the civilian migration.

For a state espionage operation whose opponents include well-funded intelligence agencies, keeping its tooling sealed against that possibility is a rational, if forward-looking, choice. Kaspersky's own reading is that the group wants to hide its later-stage payloads.

It does not, however, hide the malware where it runs; the post-quantum layer protects data in transit, and Kaspersky's analysis of the malware itself laid the whole exchange bare. Kaspersky says the work points to a dedicated developer, and the rest of the toolkit supports that view: ClientHub uses the SNOW stream cipher, a first for Lazarus according to Kaspersky, and copies headers sent by Chromium-based browsers to blend in.

Kaspersky believes the focus on software firms, the only sector hit in both SyncHole and FlashHole, reflects an appetite for source code that can be mined for new vulnerabilities. It also distinguishes FlashHole's espionage from a parallel cluster of attacks built on Lazarus's COPPERHEDGE backdoor that appears to be about making money.

For potential defenders, the lesson is the delivery rather than the cryptography: a convincing fake résumé and a trusted security plugin. Kaspersky's advice, which also promotes its own products, covers verifying unexpected links even when they lead to polished professional sites, patching quickly, removing unneeded components, restricting user privileges, and watching connections to cloud services such as GitHub and Dropbox that can double as command channels.

Since the post-quantum layer does nothing to hide what the malware does on the machine itself, capable endpoint protection software remains the realistic place to catch it. Whether its newly-found AI-assisted approach is a game changer, however, remains to be seen.

articles.headline: JD Vance fires back at Obama over Cheesecake Factory dig: ‘Super elitist’
keyFacts: Vice President JD Vance criticized Barack Obama for comparing the White House look to a Cheesecake Factory run by Saddam Hussein.
Vance claimed that Obama's comments demonstrate he is elitist and that Democrats are divorced from actual Americans.
Obama made the decor comparison at an Ohio event before later stating at an Atlanta rally that he enjoyed the restaurant.
body: Vice President JD Vance fired back at Barack Obama Thursday after the former president likened the current White House look to that of a Cheesecake Factory run by Saddam Hussein.
“I didn’t fully get it. I kind of like the Cheesecake Factory,” Vance said of Obama’s jab at a Texas town hall event hosted by Fox News’ Jesse Watters.
“I think it’s like a good example of how Obama, without even trying to be, just can’t help himself from being super elitist,” the vice president argued.
“Remember, this is the guy who said that people who wanted good jobs were ‘clinging to their guns and their religion,’ as if God and the Second Amendment were something to be ashamed of,” he added.
In attempting to mock President Trump, Vance said Obama “drove home how divorced the Democrats are from actual Americans.”
Obama unleashed the decor diss Saturday while stumping for Democrats in Ohio, as he accused Trump of spending more time sprucing up the White House than helping Americans.
“I mean, I don’t know if you’ve noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovations,” Obama said. “He should be on HGTV.”
“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”

Watters noted that Obama seemingly backpedaled on his criticism during a rally in Atlanta on Wednesday, where he insisted as “the father of two daughters” the Cheesecake Factory was “my jam for about a decade.”
“See, that’s exactly the point, though … he realized, ‘Oh, a lot of the people we want to vote for us actually like the Cheesecake Factory,’” Vance explained.
The veep added that the establishment is “the weirdest restaurant to hate on.”
“The menu is like 75 pages long, so there’s something for everybody,” he joked.
“I just don’t understand. Like, there are restaurants I can imagine beating up on – not the Cheesecake Factory,” Vance said. “Leave us alone, Barack!”
Watters joked that the network’s next town hall will be held inside a Cheesecake Factory.

articles.headline: PC chip plunge wipes out a quarter of Intel’s value
keyFacts: Intel share prices fell by nearly a quarter on Thursday following a reported decline in PC processor sales.
CEO Lip Bu Tan said the PC chip market will shrink by 12 percent next year due to memory shortages and higher prices.
Intel executives admitted the company may struggle to meet short- and long-term demand for server CPUs because of supply shortages.
body: Intel’s share price sank by almost a quarter on Thursday after the company revealed a deep dip in sales of PC processors.

The rout began after the silicon-slinger posted Q3 results that included some nice numbers, such as a 21 percent year on year revenue jump to $16.5 billion, helped by 78 percent growth for datacenter and AI products, and gross margins of 43 percent. The revenue number was at the high end of Intel’s revenue guidance of $15.8-16.8 billion, and the gross margin beat its predictions by two points.

Outweighing those upsides was a decline in revenue for client computing and physical AI products, which saw incoming cash reach $8.1 billion but fall five percent year-over-year and nine percent decline from last quarter.

In prepared remarks [PDF] published to coincide with Intel’s earnings announcement, CEO Lip Bu Tan said “In recent weeks, our customers began signaling a PC slowdown based on memory prices and availability. Year-to-date system end-point prices have increased significantly placing additional pressure on already limited IT budgets.”

“The pace of the PC correction has accelerated over the last two months, as our OEM partners are aggressively managing inventory to match the softer sell through,” he added, before predicting that the market for PC chips will shrink by 12 percent next year and remain tough “until memory availability and prices begin to normalize.”
Which may not be for years, given Korean memory-maker SK Hynix this week predicted that memory shortages will persist until the year 2030. Intel’s biggest business is therefore in trouble.
AI and Xeons riding to a rocky rescue
Tan tried to give investors reasons to be cheerful, by saying Intel sees a “resurgence in demand for CPU” sparked by customers’ desire for computing systems that consume less energy.
“Increasingly, energy efficiency is becoming the most important metric for the AI infrastructure build-out,” he said.

That matters, Tan argued, because “While GPUs are great at ‘thinking tasks,’ deterministic CPUs are far more efficient at ‘finding’ tasks. While a GPU reasoning query can run as high as multiple watt-hours of energy, a single CPU-based query could cost only joules of energy.”
The CEO reasoned that lower energy consumption is important in the context of agentic AI – the idea that we will all soon run many autonomous agents to handle personal and professional scutwork.

“Applying even conservative estimates to the total number of digital agents, and agents serviced per CPU, it is easy to anticipate a massive dollar and unit TAM [total addressable market] for CPUs over the coming five years,” Tan said. “By our estimates, server CPU TAM, largely driven by agentic workloads, could increase as much as 5X from where it is today, from $40B to more than $200B over five years.”
But during its earnings call, Intel execs admitted it may struggle to cash in on that boom in the short and longer term as the company struggles to source key supplies like silicon wafers.

Asked if Intel can meet demand for server CPUs and if investors should therefore expect further growth in datacenter product sales early in Intel’s next financial year, chief financial officer Dave Zinsner declined to offer any guidance.

“There is going to be a strong driver of demand for CPUs,” he demurred. “We see that continuing all through next year. We are working on the supply side of the equation to make sure that we can meet what customers need. We will likely not fully meet what they require, but I think we are going to be in a more challenging situation in the first half of the year than we are in the second half.”

Intel is trying to shift production around its fleet of fabs so it can crank out as much silicon as possible and will even devote some PC chip production capacity to datacenter products. But overall, Chipzilla is clearly in a spot of bother.

CEO Lip Bu Tan said his plan to “rebuild” Intel will be “a multiyear journey” and insisted “We have made enormous strides in these 18 months, including a dramatic re-sizing of our workforce, eliminating middle management and bureaucracy, streamlining our executive ranks and establishing an almost entirely new leadership team.”

He pointed to strong progress on Intel’s manufacturing processes that will bring it closer to parity with TSMC, meaning its own products will become more potent while the company’s foundry business also becomes more attractive.
And he said that Intel has restored an “engineering-centric culture” that will help the company to improve.
But the CEO also admitted “I am disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter.”
“We face near term challenges, including manufacturing supply shortages, the unprecedented memory crunch, and the resulting softness in PC demand. But I remain confident in our path forward.”

Investors did not share that confidence. Intel’s shares started the day at $92.96 apiece. Immediately after the company announced its results, shares sank to $73. At the time of writing, after-hours trading has seen the price reach $70.87, a 23.7 percent slump. ®

articles.headline: Vance urges DOJ investigation into alleged gender transition letter for 11-year-old
keyFacts: Vice President JD Vance encouraged a Texas mother to have her staff contact the DOJ to investigate a letter sent to her child about gender transition.
During a Fox News town hall, Vance criticized Texas Democrat James Talarico regarding his past legislative record and stances on transgender issues for minors.
Fox News host Jesse Watters stated that the network would conduct a journalistic investigation into the letter sent to the eleven-year-old.
body: Vice President JD Vance encouraged a Texas mother to talk to his staff about getting the Department of Justice to investigate an alleged letter sent to her 11-year-old daughter about transitioning genders without her parents’ knowledge.

Rebekah Smith of Fort Worth, Texas, brought up the letter in a question she posed to the vice president during a town hall that aired Thursday night on Fox News. Vance gave his honest response, calling the person who wrote and sent the letter a “pervert.”

“I don’t know who sent that letter to your child,” he said , “but I think the person who sends a letter to an 11-year-old about gender transition, what I call that in my family is a pervert, and that person ought to go to prison.”
In his response, Vance connected the anecdote to Texas Democrat James Talarico , who has faced scrutiny over his stance on gender transitions during his Senate campaign.
“He’ll probably defend the right of the person sending the letter,” Vance said of Talarico, “not the right of the parent who is rightfully creeped out by this.”

“James Talarico, who does have a weird fascination with trans kids, when he says that he wants to support trans kids, what he’s actually saying is that he wants to make it impossible for you to protect your children,” he said. “James Talarico has actually called it abusive when parents try to prevent their children from transitioning.”

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , who’s also running for the same Senate seat, has launched extensive attacks against Talarico over transgenderism while the Democratic candidate has been accused of flip-flopping on his position. Talarico has distanced himself from past comments he made about transgender issues, but his legislative record shows past opposition to state restrictions.

Talarico, serving in 2023 as a Texas state representative, voted against a bill that prohibited certain gender transition surgeries, puberty blockers, and hormone treatments for minors. The measure ultimately passed and took effect in September 2023.

If elected to the Senate, Talarico said he will support a federal ban on transgender surgeries for minors. He argued that the state ban was “overly broad” and threatened to take away hormone treatments for nontransgender patients, which is why he voted against it three years ago.
The Texas Democrat also walked back his previous comments on transgender athletes competing in women’s sports, saying it shouldn’t come at the cost of “safety or fairness.”

Meanwhile, Vance is one of many Republicans making the case that Talarico “has fought hard to protect” people pushing gender ideology, while Paxton has prosecuted individuals and institutions providing or promoting so-called gender-affirming care.
“Why are you going around and trying to convince children to transition their gender? That is sick and disgusting,” Vance said. “None of us signed up for it, and we’ve got to fight back.”
TRUMP AND VANCE OFFER GLIMPSE OF MAGA’S FUTURE ON MIDTERM CAMPAIGN TRAIL
The vice president advocated for the Republican state attorney general in the sit-down interview five days before the election.

Before Vance mentioned a possible DOJ investigation in relation to the letter, Fox News host Jesse Watters said the conservative news outlet would lead a journalistic investigation into the “perverted letter.”

articles.headline: How To Find The Three-Faced Puppet In Phantom Blade Zero – Triple Threat Guide
