Defeating the three-phase boss Yucong rewards players with the Freezing Chaos sword and the Chaos Iron Fragment II.
body: Are you scouring the Wulin in search of the Three-Faced Puppet in Phantom Blade Zero ? This foe might be one of the toughest that you face early in the campaign. If you achieve victory, you're bound to wonder where your quarry went. Our guide discusses everything you need to know about this opponent and the Triple Threat quest. That said, bear in mind that there will be spoilers ahead.
In This Article
The Three-Faced Puppet boss battle - Weeping Creek Valley
Triple Threat - Learn the Three-Faced Puppet’s identity
Mirrorwood - Winter Wonderland and the Blazing Edge
Yucong - The triple-phase boss battle in the Crimson Forest
Triple Threat conclusion and reward
The Three-Faced Puppet boss battle - Weeping Creek Valley

Your first encounter against the Three-Faced Puppet takes place in Weeping Creek Valley, less than an hour or so after starting the campaign. As you make your way across the cliffside section, you’ll see a ladder that descends to a ledge with a curious-looking statue. The bell right next to it is called The Lady’s Rift.

Interacting with the statue teleports you to a temple where a boss fight awaits. The Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet in Phantom Blade Zero is a tenacious opponent. She will frequently teleport, emerging from rifts to strike you. You need to time your dodges and parries right to avoid damage.
Since this is fairly early in the game, you don’t need to beat her just yet. You can come back later if you wish once you’ve upgraded your weapons and increased your maximum health .

Note: At the very least, try to defeat the boss in The Lady’s Rift before you enter the Mirage Estate. That’s the location that you go to after visiting all four Serpent Houses , and it’s pretty much the tail-end of the campaign.
The Lady's Rift bell/statue (left) leads to your first encounter with the Three-Faced Puppet (right).
Triple Threat - Learn the Three-Faced Puppet’s identity

Once you’ve defeated the Three-Faced Puppet, you’ll receive the Triple Threat quest. It tells you that you must learn the Three-Faced Puppet’s identity. You can try to scour the world for clues, including locations like the Mandate Encampment and the Mountain of Imprisonment , as they have portals that lead to the domain of the Three-Eyed Puppet.
However, the place that you should visit is actually the aforementioned Mirage Estate. Explore the sprawling complex and look for the Memory Flowers of the Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet:
I. The Wandering Healer - In the Training Grounds after you beat Yuding, the No. 12 Crescent Blade Puppet.
II. Frost and Chaos - On an altar in the Mourning Hall where you fight Qiu Feng, the Crimson Boneblade.
III. Three Souls as One - At the end of a corridor in Leng Tu’s study. Interact with a device to make the scroll move, which reveals a hidden passageway.

Note: After discovering all three Memory Flowers, you’re told to return to the Mirrorwood Entrance--one of the central bells in the Crimson Forest. Do just that and avoid proceeding to the game’s point of no return.
From left to right: The Memory Flowers. in the Training Grounds, Mourning Hall, and Leng Tu's Study
Mirrorwood - Winter Wonderland and the Blazing Edge

Changes happened in the Crimson Forest when you stepped foot in the Mirage Estate. Parts of the region are now covered in snow, and you should be able to walk across previously frozen rivers and ponds.

As for the Triple Threat quest, your goal is to defeat the Three-Faced Puppet. She’s in the northeastern corner of the zone, where you fought Bai Chilian earlier in the campaign, and you'll need to use the Blazing Edge to take her out.
The Blazing Edge is a special Soul Temper for the Sanguine Reach that requires two components, both of which are found in Meigu Lake:
One component is a reward for defeating the Gold-Masked One/Man in Black in the Long Pillar to the east.
The other component is dropped by a boss named Zhu Yuan, who’s located in the depths of the Sha-Chi Tower .

Once you have the Soul Temper item, use it to reforge the Sanguine Reach into the Blazing Edge. Make sure to level it up and pick a few accessories that boost fire damage and burn buildup, too. When you’re ready and you have the Blazing Edge equipped, go to where the boss is waiting for you.
The snow-covered Crimson Forest has new loot, enemies, and explorable locations.
Yucong - The triple-phase boss battle in the Crimson Forest

How fitting is it that you’re battling the Three-Faced Puppet, and the encounter itself has three phases. The first is mostly similar to how the Weeping Creek Valley encounter played out. The boss, Yucong (in her Steel Mask form), spins and teleports to strike you.

The second phase is when things get a bit more hectic. She will alternate among her three identities: Steel Mask (stronger attacks), Frost Mask (freeze buildup), and Chaos Mask (flames that deplete both health and sha-chi).

The third phase is when the challenge ramps up considerably. Yucong will split into not one, not two, but three entities, each utilizing their respective specialty. If you’re unprepared, you’re going to get consistently smacked around, frozen, and shadow-scorched. Try to focus on one target at a time
Face Yucong (left) and shatter the masked one for eternity (right).
Triple Threat conclusion and reward

Defeating the Three-Faced Puppet for good nets you the Freezing Chaos. It’s a one-handed sword that has a unique perk, as it lets you alternate between Yucong's three types of states/damage afflictions.
You also receive the Chaos Iron Fragment II. If you already have the other component, you’ll acquire the Chaos Twin Daggers, the Soul Temper material for the Sanguine Twin.

That does it for our guide on how to complete th Triple Threat quest. If you’re still on the lookout for other goodies at this stage of the campaign, then we encourage you to collect all Soul Temper items .
Join Soul as he faces numerous threats in the Wulin and be sure to check out more tips in our Phantom Blade Zero guides hub .

articles.headline: Israel’s final election results show neither Netanyahu nor rival can immediately form government
keyFacts: Neither Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor his rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc won the 61 parliamentary seats needed to form a government.
Arab minority parties won a combined 19 seats, but both leading blocs ruled out forming a government with them.
President Isaac Herzog will receive certified results next Wednesday and choose a candidate to form a government.
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc won 53 seats in Israel’s 120-member Knesset, or parliament, results released by election officials on Thursday showed, well below the 68 it had controlled at its peak in the previous parliament.
The bloc supporting Netanyahu’s main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, won 48 seats in an extremely tight election race, meaning neither secured the 61 seats needed to form a government.
The count is complete, but the results still need to be certified and submitted to President Isaac Herzog next Wednesday.
Herzog will then consult with party chairs and choose a candidate who he thinks has the best chance to form a government.

Parties led by Israel’s Arab minority made historic gains, winning a combined 19 seats in a race in which Palestinians with Israeli citizenship headed to the polls in record numbers Tuesday, many hoping to oust Netanyahu and far-right members of his coalition, including Bezalel Smotrich, his finance minister, and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.

Both leading blocs have ruled out the possibility of forming a government with the two main Arab parties, Ra’am and the Joint List. But their rise as potential kingmakers has brought the complex realities faced by Palestinian Israeli nationals into fresh focus.

Ahead of the election, Netanyahu and other members of his coalition amplified allegations of foreign election interference, referring Arab parties to the domestic security service, the Shin Bet, for investigation over allegations of Qatari intervention.

Qatar denied the allegations. Mansour Abbas, the head of Ra’am, said his party had “no connection” to such conduct and urged a full investigation. He also accused Netanyahu of a “campaign of incitement and delegitimization” against Arab citizens.

Dean Livne, the acting director general of Israel’s Central Elections Committee, said in a published letter sent to a member of parliament that there was “no basis for allegations of systematic violations of electoral integrity.”
Before the election, both Netanyahu and Eisenkot ruled out forming a government with the Arab parties.

But Yair Golan, the head of the smaller left-wing Democrats party, called for a government formed “in partnership” with Arab parties. “We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” he said Wednesday on X.

The majority of Palestinians with Israeli citizenship are the descendants of those who remained within what became Israel during the war that led to the country’s founding in 1948. At the time, hundreds of thousands more fled or were expelled from their homes.

articles.headline: Newsmax Host Puts Ken Paxton On The Spot With 1 Blunt Question
keyFacts: Newsmax host Rob Finnerty questioned Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton about an ad showing Republicans who refuse to vote for him.
Paxton stated that the featured voters do not represent the Republican majority and claimed opponent James Talarico makes up corruption allegations.
Recent polls show Paxton trailing Talarico in a race next week that could decide control of the U.S. Senate.
body: The Republican nominee for the U.S. Senate in Texas, Ken Paxton, was grilled in friendly territory on Thursday after some Republicans said they won’t vote for him in the midterms.
Speaking with Newsmax host Rob Finnerty, Paxton watched an ad from his opponent, James Talarico, featuring self-identified Republicans saying they won’t vote for the GOP nominee.
“I’m a Republican. And I’m passing on Ken Paxton,” each of the GOPers in the ad said.

“OK, you can add Karl Rove to that list. George W. Bush’s brother said he’s voting for Talarico. So did his daughter, one of the twins. These are the guys who want to trans everything. What’s your reaction to that?” Finnerty said.
Paxton said he wasn’t sure how long the people featured in the ad had been Republicans and that he didn’t believe they represented the majority of GOP voters.

“And obviously James Talarico can’t prove any of what he’s saying. He doesn’t want to talk about his record or my record; ‘Let’s talk about something else called corruption that I make up’ that has never been proven, just like it wasn’t proven with President Trump,” Paxton said.

Recent polls show Paxton narrowly trailing Talarico in a race that could decide control of the Senate. Should Talarico prevail next week, he would be the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate in Texas since Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.

articles.headline: A ghost story in the nation's Capitol
keyFacts: A reporter fell on Capitol stairs directly in front of Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau while attempting to ask a question.
The reporter avoided injury by rolling, but Trudeau departed without answering the question about baseball.
Capitol lore holds that the ghost of former Representative William Taulbee, shot by a journalist in 1890, trips reporters on staircases.
body: They always ask if I felt something. "Across your foot? Your shin?" My shin?
"Yeah. Your ankle. Did you feel it?" Not really. But before I respond, they ask again.
What was it like?" they inquired. "Or did you just fall?" Then they speculated I might be clumsy.
Hmmph. Clumsy. I truly don’t think so.
REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS BRACES FOR POST-ELECTION GAME OF MUSICAL CHAIRS AS LEADERSHIP BATTLES LOOM

Oh. I fall like everyone else. I work out daily. I’ve taken a couple of tumbles on predawn runs in Alexandria, Virginia. You never know when one of those sidewalk snakes will slither up from the asphalt and nip you on the ankle. I used to snow ski. I studied martial arts for years and hold a second degree black belt.
Clumsy? Nah.
"But, what do you think it was?" they follow up. Well, I have my theories.
I was a little tired that day. I noted the lip on the small staircase near the Memorial Door of the U.S. Capitol where I may have caught the edge of my brown loafers.

I remember my shoes. Rubber soles. Slight scuff on the toes. Perfectly matched with my crisp tan summer suit. Not quite an "Obama" tan suit. But appropriate for summer. And I thought at least reasonably dapper for traipsing around the U.S. Capitol and covering Congress on a sweltering July day.

Was it the shoes? My fatigue? Or how about my haste to "get the story." I spotted then-Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and his small coterie of aides and a security detail descending a spiral staircase after a meeting with then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi. D-Calif.
I would try to ask Trudeau a question.

No. This really doesn’t have anything to do with Trudeau. Or the fact that I recalled that there was a picture of him, aged about 14 or 15, at Olympic Stadium in Montreal, rooting for the Expos. He’s there with his father — the most storied of all Canadian prime ministers — the late Pierre Trudeau.

Of course, the Expos no longer play in Montreal. They don’t play at all. They moved to Washington in 2005 and are now the Nationals. And this was before the tariff wars. Montreal has been bereft of Major League Baseball ever since.
What would Youppi! Say?
Look him up, kids.

No, there wasn’t something across my shin or ankle. I didn’t feel anything. I was there, on those steps, in the U.S. Capitol, because I’m a baseball fan. And I found out that Justin Trudeau watched those old Montreal Expos teams in the 1980s. Stocked with Andre Dawson, Warren Cromartie and Steve Rogers. And even though Trudeau was there to discuss affairs of state with Pelosi and others, I was there to ask him about the national pastime.
Ironic, I know, to pose such an interrogative to a Canadian .

However, the reason was that there was a report that the Tampa Bay Rays might consider splitting their season each year between Florida and Montreal. Big league baseball would return to Quebec. It would be international news if Trudeau commented. It would appear on Fox. FS1. ESPN. TSN in Canada. And Montreal — famously robbed of perhaps winning the World Series in 1994 with the best team in the game that year because of the player’s strike — might have a shot again at baseball glory.
But journalism is like baseball. A game of failure. You sometimes swing and miss. You’re doing great if you’re successful three out of ten times.
THE HITCHHIKER'S GUIDE TO WHY REMOVING ILHAN OMAR FROM CONGRESS COULD BE HARDER THAN TRUMP EXPECTS
And sometimes, in journalism, the question is never asked.
That was this day. On those steps. Questions about the Rays and Montreal were muted. All because of whatever got me.
Absolutely got me.
I stepped toward Trudeau, mumbled something about Tampa Bay and bought it.
I fell on those steps. Directly in front of the Canadian Prime Minister. On the hard Capitol marble.
I quickly realized I was about to fall. With a microphone in one hand, I couldn’t catch myself. I was confident I’d break a wrist or a hand if I tried to catch myself.
So, I just went with it and fell.
And because I studied martial arts for all of those years from Master Kim and Master Yang back at the Tae Kwon Do dojang, I knew how to fall without hurting myself.
I rolled onto my right shoulder toward Trudeau.
My feeling flew up absurdly high in the air.
"Oh Chad! Oh Chad! Oh Chad!" hollered my photographer, Robert Fetzer. "Chad!"
Trudeau stopped briefly. But I leaped to my feet after the roll, hoping he might say something about baseball.
I struck out. And Trudeau departed.
"But what tripped you?" they ask. "Were you all right?"
Physically, I was fine. Mentally, kind of garbled. I’ve worked daily at the U.S. Capitol for decades. I had a sneaking suspicion of what got me. Or better yet, who?

In the latter years of the 19th Century, Rep. William Taulbee, D-Ky., did not get along with reporter Charles Kincaid. Taulbee thought Kincaid wasn’t an honest broker, writing screeds about his personal affairs.
Taulbee was tall, towering over the diminutive Kincaid. Taulbee was known to sometimes physically pummel Kincaid.

Taulbee was out of federal office. But Kincaid knew Taulbee would be at the Capitol. Kincaid packed a pistol with him. And on Feb. 28, 1890, the reporter shot the Bluegrass Congressman square in the eye.
Taulbee leaked blood all the way down the House’s "Y" staircase, the plasma blending with marble. Through a miracle of chemistry, the splotches are still visible today.
The Kentucky Democrat succumbed to his injuries 11 days later.
It probably goes without saying that Taulbee does not like the congressional press corps. And, so, his phantasm is known to lurk around the Capitol.
Sometimes low bridging reporters on ornate staircases.
"What tripped you?" they ask.
And before I can answer, my inquisitors jump to a conclusion, albeit an interrogative one.
"Was it a ghost ?" they giddily exclaim, like they had just figured out Final Jeopardy.
As I say, I have my theories. I’ll let you come to your own conclusions.
But I don’t want to trip you up.

articles.headline: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work
keyFacts: David Durman, a nontheistic Humanist and university administrator, secured a religious exemption from using AI in his workplace.
Durman stated that AI threatens human well-being, creativity, and the critical thinking required to be a moral actor.
The University of Kentucky stated it reviews accommodation requests individually and determined Durman could perform his duties without AI.
body: Pope Leo XIV has decried AI as a threat to human dignity, but it’s not just the devoutly faithful who might worry about how AI squares with their beliefs. David Durman, a nontheistic Humanist, recently secured a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.

“Humanism is a collection of beliefs about the human experience and how humans interact with the world,” Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, told TechCrunch. It centers on “human well-being and flourishing, both individually and collectively […] and implores a person to try to improve both their well-being and their flourishing as well as the others around them.”

As he watched AI grow more popular in daily life, Durman sought out the American Humanist Association (AHA) — a nonprofit advancing secular humanism — to investigate how he could gain legal protections against having to use AI at work. He believes that using the technology runs counter to his beliefs.

“The way we become moral actors for ourselves and for others is through the active application of our minds, and the diminishing of that [through AI use] is going to necessarily have a negative impact on our ability to do so,” he said, reflecting on how overreliance on AI might affect critical thinking.

In a statement published by the AHA earlier this week, Durman wrote, “AI is interfering with people’s ability to earn a living, the environmental costs spell disaster for humanity and our planet, and its supplanting and theft of human creativity threaten elements of our culture like art and literature that make society flourish.”
Humanism is not anti-religious, but it tends to appeal to people who are skeptical of a god or other supernatural power yet still seek a scientific and moral framework to ground themselves in.

“Concern about AI and human dignity can run through several different faiths and traditions, whether that’s Catholic teachings, or Universalism, or Humanism, and we want Humanists or nontheists to know that they fall into these categories — that they are also protected by the law at work,” Alexandria Huiskens, Staff Attorney at the AHA, told TechCrunch.

Durman is the first Humanist to secure workplace accommodations that allow him to abstain from AI use, and one of the first people to publicly discuss their pursuit of these protections. He was inspired to seek them when he read that Erin Maus, a Unitarian Universalist and software engineer, was able to secure similar protections for herself.

“For me, this was about me and my convictions,” Durman said. “I’m obviously not trying to tell people how to think or feel… But I do hope that it encourages people who have similar concerns to pursue not necessarily religious exemption, but pursue their concerns to the best of their ability where they feel is the most appropriate.”

University of Kentucky spokesperson Jay Blanton told TechCrunch that the institution reviews requests for religious accommodations on an individual basis, considering the employee’s job responsibilities and the circumstances of the request.

“In this case, the university determined that an accommodation could be provided while allowing the employee to continue performing the essential functions of their position,” Blanton said in a statement. “As technology and job responsibilities evolve, accommodations may be reviewed to ensure they remain reasonable and workable.”

Maus’ situation is especially unusual, since it has become rare for software engineers to write code without any AI assistance. But in Durman’s administrative role, in which he supports researchers applying for grants, he has not been required to use AI at work. Like many workers across fields, some of his colleagues and leadership have recommended that employees try out these tools, so he sought to secure his exemption now, in case the suggestion becomes a mandate in the future.
“I hope that if [others] have similar feelings, that they feel encouraged to pursue some kind of resolution,” Durman said.

articles.headline: Here’s Why You’re About to See More Ads in Google’s AI Overviews
keyFacts: Alphabet said search ad revenue growth slowed because user queries shifted to AI Overviews and AI Mode, which suffer from lower monetization.
Google is expanding ads in AI Mode to 10 new countries and launching multiturn ads in the US for follow-up queries with commercial relevance.
SEO expert Lily Ray said the changes will make it harder for users to find publisher articles and cause further declines in organic web traffic.
body: If you happened to listen to Alphabet’s quarterly earnings call on Wednesday, you might have heard that searches are up, but ad revenue is down. According to Google Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler, search ad revenue growth slowed in the third quarter of 2026 because user queries are migrating to AI Overviews and AI Mode, which suffer from “lower monetization.”

You actually know how this works. When you type a question into Google, a summarized AI response often appears immediately, reducing the classic ad-clicking behavior further down on the page, which generates Google’s core revenue.

Now, the tech giant is expanding how and where we see ads when using AI Mode during searches. Google is scaling ads in AI Mode to 10 new countries (including Australia, Canada, India, Kenya and Singapore), with plans to launch in Brazil, Mexico and the UK later this year.
More from CNET

In the US, Google is launching what it calls “multiturn ads,” allowing ads to appear directly within follow-up queries in AI Mode when a search or conversation has “commercial relevance.” Take, for example, if you start a search with “How does a smart fridge work,” and follow up with “What are the best-selling smart fridges?” You could then see refrigerator ads in sections labeled “sponsored.”

Google said that “multiturn ads” can better target what a user wants in a product because AI Mode gathers more information during a back-and-forth conversation. Ads can also appear on initial AI Mode queries, not just after follow-up questions, and sometimes ads won’t appear at all if there doesn’t appear to be purchase intent, according to Google.
But as Google relies more on AI Mode and AI Overview, there’ll be less reason to click on content links “below the fold,” meaning content that sits out of view until a reader scrolls down a web page.

Lily Ray, a well-known SEO expert and founder of Algorythmic, told CNET that it’s going to become harder to use Google to find articles from preferred publishers and articles you want to read directly from a website. “You’ll have to dig deeper and look outside of Google’s products,” Ray said via email.

According to Ray, Google’s AI tools aren’t designed to give you the exact link you’re looking for. Still, you don’t have to rely on AI Mode or AI Overviews to get search results. You can also scroll down to the search results the old-fashioned way or use a web filter to use Google as a list of links. She also recommends setting up your favorite publications as “preferred sources” (instructions here) so you can see more of those pages cited in your personalized results.
“Unless you’re satisfied with AI answers directly on Google, you’re going to need to start evolving your own search behavior to find the websites you’re looking for,” Ray said.
AI, advertising and traffic

Google is still the largest search engine in the world, accounting for nearly 90% of the global search engine market. In fact, the company said its year-over-year query volume growth in the third quarter was the fastest over the past five years.
But beginning with the launch of AI Overviews in May 2024, Google’s reliance on AI has slowed advertising.

The impact has been even more devastating for online publishers — ranging from major newspapers and digital media sites to brands and trade associations — driving an unprecedented decline in website traffic. AI Overviews now appear on nearly half of Google search queries, with a corresponding 61% drop in raw traffic volume to other pages. Google is effectively scraping publisher information, summarizing it and satisfying the user before they leave the search results page. That’s why it’s often referred to as the “zero-click” crisis.
“AI Mode and AI Overviews answer questions directly in Google’s interface, so there’s less reason for people to click on publishers,” Ray said.

AI Overviews are summary boxes at the top of a traditional search results page, while AI Mode is a conversational interface designed for ongoing dialogue and research. You can access AI Mode directly by selecting the AI Mode button at the far right of the search bar on the Google home page, or by selecting AI Mode in the horizontal menu near the top of other Google pages.

When you use AI Mode, you won’t get an AI Overview or a long list of links to other websites offering more information. Instead, AI Mode provides “more advanced reasoning and ways of interacting” with a conversational approach. For instance, if I use AI Mode and ask, “Where can I see the northern lights?” I get a map and a list of various locations with pros and cons for each. In regular search mode, I get an AI Overview at the top and, below that, pages of links to websites related to my query.

Ray said that with more ads, there’s going to be an even greater decline in organic click-through rates — in publishing speak, that’s the percentage of people who actually click on a natural, nonpaid search engine result, out of the total number of people who simply saw the headline on the page. Not only will the AI text answer your question, but Google will now aggressively route you toward advertisers rather than publisher links.
“Like many things in Google Search, it means that if you’re not participating in Google Ads, it’s going to be harder and harder to get that traffic organically,” said Ray.

articles.headline: Reddit will switch to a 'logged-in only experience'
keyFacts: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman announced that the website will transition to a logged-in only experience, starting with tests outside the US before a global rollout.
Huffman stated that the change aims to reduce reliance on search traffic affected by AI summaries and protect Reddit's valuable data corpus.
Despite reporting revenue growth, Reddit's share price dropped following a lower-than-expected forecast for the next quarter.
body: Reddit will become a "logged-in only experience," and the company plans to move fast, beginning testing soon in regions outside the US before flipping the switch globally.

The popular community website—home to a great many official and unofficial gaming message boards—lost one million search engine referrals per week on average in October, CEO Steve Huffman said on an investor call today.

The culprit, of course, was AI. A Google search that once might have led someone to a 14-year-old Reddit thread containing the answer to a rare household cleaning problem is now likely to present that answer in an AI summary, no click required.
"Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the internet," Huffman said during a Q&A.

The CEO emphasized, however, that most of Reddit's revenue (over 80%) comes from logged-in and app users, and said that the company will focus on establishing the site as "a direct daily habit" that doesn't rely on search traffic.

Efforts cited in that direction include algorithmic feeds, improved app design and performance, AI-powered moderation tools, and "new experiences like games and visual podcasts," the latter referring to, I believe, a feature that uses generative AI to turn posts into videos.
The switch to a logged-in only experience will also help "protect access to Reddit's extremely valuable corpus of data," Huffman said.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Reddit currently has AI training arrangements with OpenAI and Google. In the Q&A portion of the call, Huffman said that Reddit has nothing to announce about those deals, but that it is in "active discussions" and that its leadership will "do what makes sense and is in the best interest for Reddit strategically and economically."

Although it reported 53% year-over-year revenue growth in its 2026 third-quarter results, as well as 16% growth in weekly active users, Reddit's share price dropped today due to a lower-than-expected forecast for the next quarter.

body: Curry Barker, the director behind the hit horror film Obsession, just published a new horror short on YouTube. The short, titled “Mama Bear,” is nearly five minutes long. articles.headline: All Trades in Probably Stolen and how to unlock them
keyFacts: Players in Probably Stolen can choose a trade at the start or adopt new ones during a run by meeting specific requirements.
Trades such as Water Trading, Winemaking, and Hydroponic Farming are unlocked through starting choices or by purchasing specific items with credits.
Other trades like Smelting are unlocked for free on Day 6 from Dr. Jackson, while Chemistry and Gunsmithing require starting roles or retired purchasers.
body: Establishing your business empire in Probably Stolen isn’t an easy task, and you can do so with the help of different Trades. When you begin your adventures, you will be able to pick a trade. However, you can also adopt new ones in the middle of a run.
That said, you’ll need to meet the conditions for unlocking the trades.
How to unlock all Trades in Probably Stolen
Every trade in Probably Stolen remains locked behind certain requirements. Some are easy to unlock, while others have more stiff requirements.

Trade How to Unlock Water Trading You can unlock it at the very start by beginning as Water Merchant. You can also buy Water Trading from the Wild for 300 Credits. Winemaking You can unlock it by buying the Retired Winemaker for 200 Credits. Hydroponic Farming You can unlock it by starting at the Hydroponic Farmer. You can also purchase the Retired Farmer for 350 Credits. Plant Genetics First, you’ll need to buy the Retired Farmer. Then, get Plant Genetics for 1,250 Credits. Chemistry You can either begin as a Chemist or buy Retired Chemist for 1,000 Credits. Gunsmithing You can begin as a Gunsmith, or get the Retired Gunsmith for 650 Credits. Smelting You’ll unlock it for free on Day 6 from Dr. Jackson. Rat Ranching You can begin as a Rat Wrangler, or buy Ranching for 750 Credits. articles.headline: 'I'm built differently' - Hamilton defiant over extending F1 career into 2030s
keyFacts: Lewis Hamilton stated that extending his Formula 1 career into the 2030s is realistic because he is built differently.
Hamilton said his current focus is ensuring Ferrari secures second place in the Constructors' Championship rather than his position in the drivers' standings.
Hamilton's contract with Ferrari runs until the end of the 2027 season, with an option to extend for an additional year.
body: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says he 'is built differently' amid defiance over extending his F1 career into 2030s

Lewis Hamilton insists the idea of him continuing his F1 career into the 2030 is realistic; the 41-year-old wants to compete in F1's first race in Rwanda; watch every session of the Mexico City GP with Friday's practice sessions at 6.30pm and 10pm, live on Sky Sports F1
Thursday 29 October 2026 23:48, UK
Lewis Hamilton insisted he "is built differently" as he continued to rule out extending his Formula 1 career into the 2030s.

Following the announcement earlier in October that Africa will return to the F1 calendar at some point in the 2030s with a race in Rwanda, Hamilton had said he hoped he would be able to compete in the first grand prix on the continent since 1993.

Given Hamilton turns 42 in January and will be 45 at the start of the 2030 F1 season, at which point it is far from certain the circuit in Rwanda will be ready, it was initially unclear how seriously his comments should be taken.

- Mexico City GP Schedule | F1 2026 standings | F1 2026 calendar

- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺

But quizzed on the topic on Thursday ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, the seven-time world champion said: "I mean, firstly, you've never had anyone like me here in the 70 years [of the sport's history], so I feel that I'm built differently.

"Of course, there are challenges up ahead that I can't foresee that come with age. But along this way, along this journey, there have been so many preconceived ideas about the fact that your reaction time drops off.
"Did you see my reaction in the last race? My reaction is faster than some of the youngest people here. There are lots of tools that you can utilise to continue to keep yourself, your mind sharp.

"I guess as long as you're willing to sacrifice everything, which I am right now, I can't say in four years whether I want to continue to do what I'm doing. But I love what I'm doing still now. I'm still all in, and I will be for the foreseeable future."
Hamilton's current contract with Ferrari is understood to run until the end of the 2027 season, with the Brit holding an option to extend for a further year should he wish to do so.

After a blockbuster move from Mercedes to Ferrari for the 2025 season, Hamilton's performances during his first year in red raised doubts, at times from the driver himself himself, over whether his skills were declining, but he has bounced back with a much-improved 2026 campaign, which included a memorable victory in Barcelona.
Hamilton continued: "Whether or not I can compete at 44 with a 20-year-old, who knows? But at 41, I can compete with a 20-year-old. So, time will tell whether I'm here in the 2030s, we'll see.
"But I never want to overstay my welcome in the sense of still not having the performance. I don't want to be driving around with that really dropped off.
"My reaction has dropped off, my driving has dropped off, and my pace has dropped off, which everyone assumed last year. But I've proved everyone wrong with that, and I'll continue to try to do so."
Hamilton's focus on Constructors', not Drivers' Championship

While Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli is set to seal the Drivers' Championship this weekend with four races to spare, Hamilton is part of an extremely tight four-way battle for second place in the standings.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell is in second, a point ahead of Hamilton, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen five points further back and the other Ferrari of Charles Leclerc three more points adrift.
Hamilton insists his focus is on ensuring Ferrari seal second in the Constructors' Championship, in which they hold a 119-point over Red Bull and McLaren, with Mercedes 133 points clear out front.

"I'm not going to say it [second in the Drivers' Championship] doesn't mean anything, but it's not something I focus on," Hamilton said. "Winning the championship is the only thing any of us really care about.
"Maybe some people do care about the other positions, but for me, my sole focus is on making sure that we secure second in the Constructors' Championship because the team deserve it.
"It's a huge boost from last year and it really is something we can build on for next year.
"In terms of finishing second, third, fourth, you want to finish first."
'The car should be good here'
Hamilton is hopeful Ferrari can deliver a strong weekend in Mexico, where many believe the turbo element of their engine, which is smaller than their rivals', could be an advantage at high altitude.
Asked about Ferrari's chances, Hamilton said: "Someone just said that it should be good for our car, and I really have no idea.
"I mean, everyone's going to be maximum downforce here. It would be an unusual experience for us all, because it's like 25 or 30 per cent less downforce than we had the last time we drove here.
"So, whether we can get the tyres switched on... the car should be good here.
"And being that we have high altitude, hopefully straight-line speed won't be as affected as it is in some of the other places where at sea level the drag is significant.
"So, I'm hoping that we are able to continue on from the strong performance we had last year and bring it into this weekend."

articles.headline: AC Milan and Inter unveil stunning images and name of new 71,500 stadium to replace San Siro
keyFacts: AC Milan and Inter Milan unveiled images and the name of their new 71,500-seater Generali Stadium, which will replace the San Siro.

body: AC Milan and Inter Milan have unveiled their brand-new 71,500-seater stadium that will replace the iconic San Siro.
The San Siro, which turned 100 years old last month, is going to be demolished once the new ground opens in 2031.
Milan and Inter unveiled their new stadium on Thursday with a series of stunning images AC Milan
The 71,500-seater ground has an X frame structure and a double curved roof AC Milan
Stunning images of Milan and Inter ‘s shared home were revealed on Thursday evening, along with the venue’s name.
The stadium will be called the Generali Stadium, with Italian insurance company Generali claiming the naming rights.
The deal is reported to be worth a whopping $725m over 20 years.
Milan and Inter unveil the Generali Stadium
Within the unveiling, the Serie A giants revealed the stadium has been designed around ‘one of football’s most iconic atmospheres’.
Foster + Partners and MANICA were behind the architecture, which features an X frame structure and a double curved roof.

Milan and Inter also wrote in their joint statement : “More than a football stadium, the project represents a long-term investment in the future of two of world football’s most historic clubs, a new home for generations of supporters, and a destination designed to contribute to the cultural, economic and urban development of the city.
“The unveiling marks an important milestone in a journey that continues to transform ambition into reality.
“It offers the first comprehensive look at a stadium designed to honour the legacy of San Siro while creating a world-class experience built for the future of football.
“The project is driven by a shared long-term vision from the Clubs and their respective owners, RedBird Capital Partners and Oaktree, part of Brookfield’s credit platform.

“It represents a defining investment in the future of both organisations, creating the infrastructure needed to support sustained sporting success, unlock new opportunities for growth, and strengthen their ability to compete and win at the highest international level.
Insurance company Generali have claimed naming rights for the Italian giants’ stadium for a reported $725m AC Milan
The club’s revealed that the Generali Stadium has been designed around ‘one of football’s most iconic atmospheres’ AC Milan

“At the same time, the project reflects a broader ambition: to contribute to the modernization of Italian football while reinforcing Milano’s position as one of Europe’s most dynamic, innovative and globally recognized cities.

“The architectural vision has been developed by Foster + Partners and MANICA, bringing together Lord Norman Foster, one of the world’s most influential contemporary architects, and David Manica, one of the leading designers of sports venues worldwide.

“Building on a collaboration that dates back to the design of London’s Wembley Stadium, the partnership combines architectural excellence and stadium expertise to create a destination rooted in Milano’s identity while looking firmly to the future.”
Why are they moving out of the San Siro?
Milan chairman Paolo Scaroni explained last year that the clubs were moving out of the San Siro as it is not fit for modern football.
The iconic ground that has been the home of the two Milan sides since 1947 has sadly not kept with the times.
Scaroni said: “For us, this a historic moment. It has taken five or six years to reach this point and we had great support from our owners RedBird.
The iconic San Siro in Milan will be demolished after 100 years Getty
“San Siro has been excluded by UEFA as a stadium for Euro 2032 – it simply doesn’t have all the facilities that are needed for modern football.
“We badly need a new stadium.
“We have always had a good relationship with Inter, so it makes sense to continue sharing the new stadium and split the costs of building and running it.”

articles.headline: Mouthwashing is getting a feature film adaptation from Sony and I need all of you to be normal about it whenever it comes out
keyFacts: Sony Pictures' Screen Gems has acquired the feature film rights to the video game Mouthwashing, according to The Hollywood Reporter.
Karyn Kusama is attached to direct the adaptation, with Matt Manfredi and Phil Hay as writers and Scott Derrickson as a producer.
The article notes that the game explores themes of corporate exploitation and sexual assault, raising questions about how it will translate to a live-action film.
body: I quite liked that there video game Mouthwashing. It had a lot to say about how corporations take advantage of their workers, it played around with character perspective to let you in on certain narrative threads and withhold others until they're taut enough to snap, and was short enough so that its misery didn't outstay its welcome. What I wasn't so fond of was much of the fandom response that came afterwards, which is why I am quite scared to say that it's getting a movie from Sony.

As shared by The Hollywood Reporter, Sony have acquired the feature film rights to Mouthwashing, attaching names both promising and apprehension inducing to it. It's being produced in part by Scott Derrickson, director of Sinister (which I liked well enough) and Doctor Strange (a wet fart sound of a movie). What is more interesting is that Karyn Kusama, director of the excellent cult classic Jennifer's Body, is attached to direct. Given the game's themes of sexual assault, which is putting it lightly, it's nice to see a woman in the director's seat.
YES, MOUTHWASHING MOVIE IS REALLY HAPPENING SOON™
You thought you could escape responsibility by turning off your console?
Produced by Sony Pictures' Screen Gems and directed by Karyn Kusama.
[image or embed]
— Critical Reflex (@cr-games.bsky.social) October 29, 2026 at 8:17 PM

The thing that loops me back around to fear is having Matt Manfredi and Phil Hay attached as writers; the pair have long worked together, but often on stinkers like Clash of the Titans, The Tuxedo, and R.I.P.D. At the very least the two of them and Kusama are frequent collaborators, having made The Invitation and Destroyer together (it probably helps that Hay and Kusama are married).

As with every single live action adaptation of a video game, I of course immediately feel that it is wholly unnecessary, and certainly think that's the case for Mouthwashing. It's a game that has minimal interactivity, much more of a walking sim than anything else. It also deeply relies on said interactivity, alongside its first-person perspective, so I'm not sure how well that would translate. And upsettingly, the game developed an uncomfortably intense fandom that has frequently treated the game's themes as a suggestion, prioritising skits and memes above a real reckoning with what it's doing. This leaves me afraid of a film adaptation. Perhaps I'll log off for the day whenever it comes out.

articles.headline: Sony is working on a film adaptation of viral indie horror game Mouthwashing
keyFacts: Sony Pictures Entertainment acquired the film rights to the indie horror game Mouthwashing from developer Wrong Organ, according to The Hollywood Reporter.

body: Sony is working on a film adaptation of viral indie horror game Mouthwashing
Karyn Kusama is attached to direct.

Indie horror game Mouthwashing is making the jump to film. Sony Pictures Entertainment has acquired the rights to the game from developer Wrong Organ, according to The Hollywood Reporter, and Karyn Kusama, director of Jennifer's Body and The Invitation, is attached to direct.

The project will be written by Matt Manfredi and Phil Hay, the screenwriters behind The Invitation, and produced by Scott Derrickson, the director of The Black Phone and Sinister. Sony is likely hoping the combination of horror talent and hit video game IP will repeat the success it saw with Resident Evil. Zach Cregger's adaptation of Capcom's survival horror series was not only a critical hit, but also a financial success.

Mouthwashing is much more grounded than Resident Evil's goofier flavor of horror. The game follows the crew of a stranded spaceship as they slowly lose their grip on reality. It isn't chock-full of jump scares, but its heavy themes and surreal imagery make it an interesting choice for a film adaptation.

The film doesn't yet have a release date, but the game has gotten a lot easier to play if you want to experience the story before you watch. Mouthwashing launched on PC in 2024 and as of today, it's also available on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S and through Xbox Game Pass.

articles.headline: Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says
keyFacts: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed that the platform is moving to a logged-in-only experience.
Huffman stated the change will improve user experience, ad targeting, data protection, and user retention.
Reddit will test the login requirement in select non-US markets during the fourth quarter.
body: In the future, you won’t be able to use Reddit without logging in.
Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed the impending change in a letter (PDF) to shareholders today about Q3 performance. He said that Reddit is shifting “to a logged-in-only experience,” adding:

Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world.
Huffman also said that the login requirement will help Reddit better retain new users.
Reddit will start testing the login requirement in “select,” non-US markets in Q4. The company will use those tests to decide what a logged-in-only Reddit will look like “globally,” per Huffman.

“Pretty much all of the major ad-based platforms have gone through this transition. We are excited and moving quickly,” the CEO added, noting Reddit’s intent to become a “direct daily habit for every Internet user.”

The impending requirement comes as Reddit search referral traffic “was down meaningfully in Q3,” Huffman wrote. The largest hit came from logged-out and web traffic, and the overall trend has continued into Q4.

“During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week. If this rate of decline continues, current trends would suggest that total DAUqs [or daily active unique users] could fall in Q4, by a low-double-digit percentage from our current base of 130 million DAUqs,” Huffman wrote.

articles.headline: Spirit Halloween 2026: The Kotaku Review
keyFacts: Kotaku reviewers RV and Zack Zwiezen visited a Spirit Halloween store to inspect various costumes, props, and displays.
The reviewers documented a mix of weird, poorly made, and notable costumes, ranging from pop culture characters to knockoffs.
The store featured various licensed and unlicensed items, including Mario characters, horror icons, and internet trend references.
body: Saturday is Halloween, and woe unto thee if you have not yet assembled your costume, because all the good stuff has been thoroughly picked over and is rapidly rising in price. I’m going as a lazy Luigi (regular overalls and green shirt, actual Luigi hat) to a Trunk or Treat this weekend where I’ll be handing out candy and tiny plastic skeletons to kids. Sometimes it’s nice not to have to care too much.

For those that do, though, there’s always Spirit Halloween. I hadn’t been to one of these in a few years, so my resident Halloween enthusiast colleague Zack Zwiezen graciously showed me around one earlier this week. Together, we took a zillion photos, and we’re here now before you with a presentation of the weirdest, worst, and most notable things we saw there. Most of it’s costumes, some of it’s other stuff, all of it is…well, I guess representative of Halloween in the U.S. in 2026.
Come take a journey with us into Spirit Halloween, three days before that sacred night:
Yoshi

Figured I’d start us off with something fairly innocuous. There was, naturally a lot of Mario at Spirit Halloween. The adult section was (weirdly) mostly Luigi, but the kids’ section had more variety. That said: I don’t know what a normal-looking Yoshi costume, to me, would be. But this specific one upset me for some reason. “Carapace gonflable incluse!” -RV
Toad
Again, I’m not sure what a normal one of these would be. You’re probably not gonna let your kid run around in just a vest on a chilly Halloween night. But this still looks wrong, somehow. -RV
Mushroom Queen

The kids’ section had an actual, branded Peach costume, so it was sort of goofy to see this unlicensed option in the adults’ section in lieu of a real Peach costume. I guess Nintendo was one of the few (very few, as we will see) companies to draw the line on licensed “sexy” versions of its characters. -RV
Joker Wall
Zack has led me to understand that a wall like this is mandatory in every Spirit Halloween store. -RV
Harry Potter aisle

My original pitch for this article was “The 10 Worst Things We Saw At Spirit Halloween” and this was going to either be top of the list, or a Dishonorable Mention at the bottom (because, while “worst” is accurate, it’s unfortunately not very fun/funny, which the rest of this list is intended to be). -RV
Pikachu or Saw
Just some environmental storytelling. -RV
Lazy PokÃ©mon
Okay, but speaking of PokÃ©mon, is this what passes for PokÃ©mon costumes these days? Just a onesie and a hood? Come on, guys, we can do better than this.
Lazy Spider-Man
Now this is just flat-out lame. Where are his pants??? This was right next to an actual, full Spider-Man suit on the rack. -RV
“Spider-Man”

Look, anyone can be a Spider-Man if they want to be, gender be damned. But I just find it funny that this was two feet away from a similarly-shaped costume of a different superhero entitled “Ladypool.” -RV
Chewbacca

Lovable Star Wars furball and loyal hero Chewbacca is not an easy character to recreate at home, but even I didnât expect the Spirit Halloween version to look so bad. At least this version looks better than the hard mask Spirit used to sell. -ZZ
Discount Vader
“25% off Helmet won’t stay shut” -Spirit Halloween
Inflatable Dinosaur
An all-time classic returns. No complaints, no notes. -RV
Big Freddy

I’m not a fan of where FNaF has gone since like, the first game, but even I have to admit this is a damn good-looking real animatronic version of a fictional animatronic. Unfortunately, it would not turn on while we were there at around 7:30 p.m. Probably should have tried again around midnight. -RV
Retro Jason

Over the many years Iâve been visiting Spirit, Iâve begun to notice a trend of famous killers getting more variants. Perhaps the oddest one Iâve spotted in recent years is a purple Jason inspired by his appearance in the infamous NES game based on the Friday the 13th Movies. Itâs cool, but how many people under 30 will even care?
Officer Dick Udown
I’m not going to linger here but wow there sure are a lot of costumes like this (cops, lewd, lewd cops). -RV
Green Oogie Boogie

Okay, so. Did you know this is a thing? I didn’t. I always thought Oogie Boogie was like, tan. A burlap sack guy. I learned last night, in the Spirit Halloween that he has effectively been rebranded in a lot of merch and even in Disney Dreamlight-freakin’-Valley as a green dude because I guess he glows under a blacklight? This is controversial and many people disagree over whether or not his greenification is a good thing. I’m joining the war on Team Burlap. -RV
20s Gangster
It’s literally the ’20s RIGHT NOW?!?!?! -RV
Big weird inflatable guy
Someone please comment on this article and explain to me what this is supposed to be because I have no idea. -RV
Buster Sword

There was a big section of weapons that included several swords not officially branded as any particular thing, but were definitely intended to read as swords from stuff like Game of Thrones, World of Warcraft, and Final Fantasy. -RV
The Backrooms Hazmat suit

This was literally the only thing I saw fromÂ The Backrooms. I think it’s really funny that they felt the need to sell something fromÂ The Backrooms but the only real costume-able thing they could come up with was a Hazmat suit. They should have made a weird chair costume or something. -RV
Dead by Daylight âDevil Faceâ

I think this costume looks pretty cool, but I feel bad for any kid or teen who wears it on Halloween night. Theyâll be forced to explain its strange origins as a variant of the Ghost Face mask seen in a video game, not the famous Scream movies. -ZZ
Definitely not Ghoul from Fallout

I pointed the costume in the first image out to Zack early on as a pretty funny attempt at a knockoff Ghoul from the Fallout TV series, only for us to stumble upon an actual branded Ghoul mask later on. -RV
Knockoff Mortal Kombat

I find it peculiar that Iâve not encountered any Mortal Kombat costumes at Spirit in recent years. It seems like between the movies, the franchise popping up in Fortnite, and the games being good this past decade, Mortal Kombat is bigger than it has been in a while. But if you want to dress up like one of the franchiseâs ninjas, youâll have to settle for a knockoff. -ZZ
Knockoff Call of Duty
Your young son can dress up as a knockoff Ghost from Call of Duty alongside his bigger brother, who is also dressed up as a knockoff Ghost from Call of Duty. Yay! -ZZ
John Halo

This and the next few on the list represent some actually pretty all right kids’ costumes we saw. I’m not sure which kids this age are super enthused about Halo, necessarily, but if they want to dress as John Halo for Halloween, more power to ’em.
Sonic
Quintessential Sonic the Hedgehog costume. A little weird, but probably cool if you’re a kid. They had Shadow, too. -RV
Zero

All right, this one is just downright adorable. Great idea for a costume, great pairing with the Jack Skellington and Sally costumes over in the adult section. Possibly the only thing we saw all evening that had everyone in our group genuinely delighted. -RV
Lamb Chop

Now, all right. I love Lamb Chop. I grew up with her, Charlie Horse, Hush Puppy, and the delightful Shari Lewis. But I gotta know: who, in 2026, is still familiar enough with and excited enough about Lamb Chop to dress up their baby as her for Halloween? My understanding was that Lamb Chop had mostly been (shamefully, regrettably) relegated to infamy as a dog toy.

However, writing this is how I learned that apparently Shari Lewis’ daughter, Mallory Lewis, has brought back her mom’s puppets on social media and (seemingly?) has fantastic politics. So maybe it’s time for Lamb Chop to make a comeback:
-RV
E.T.
On the other hand, maybe some retro things just really shouldn’t be kids’ costumes. Or costumes at all. -RV
Fall Guys
I don’t have anything smart or funny to say about these, I just thought they were genuinely quite cute, well-done costumes. This is what the Fall Guys look like! Yes! -RV
Aang
Nope nope nope nope nope nopeÂ nope.Â Why does it have to have the mask?!Â -RV
Poppy Playtime
It would be weird to not see some Poppy Playtime gear at Spirit in 2026. And there was plenty here when we visited earlier this week, though not as much as before, so it seems to be selling. -ZZ
Fortnite Wall

Over the years, Spiritâs wall of Fortnite costumes has grown and grown. But this year, I didnât spot too many new additions, and even more damning: It was still filled with costumes this close to Halloween. Have the kids moved on? -ZZ
Art the Clown Baby Outfit

Look, the babies wearing this outfit have no idea who Art the Clown is and are innocent. But the parents dressing up their kids as a murderous clown from some of the most gory horror movies in recent years should really think about why they are doing that. -ZZ
Oompa Loompa
Back to the adult costumes for some final cursed entries. I think this one is funny because we all know exactly what it’s referencing. -RV
Silly Branded Knife

I hate these dumb prop knives so much. They look tacky, ugly, and bad and donât seem like something youâd want to collect. They also seem like a bad prop for a costume unless your version of some famous slasher is branded like a NASCAR driver. -ZZ
Pizza
Sorry, is that a pizza delivery box in their hand? Is the pizza…delivering…itself?! -RV
Brainrot Characters

Itâs wild to think that for younger kids, these bizarre AI-generated nightmares are likely more famous and recognizable than a Star Wars hero or DC Comics villain. Iâm curious, though, how many kids actually buy these costumes or if this is just dudes in suits chasing trends. -ZZ
SpongeBob
A big wall of SpongeBob was the first thing we saw when we walked in. Most of these costumes are fine, even mildly funny! Like this Handsome Squidward mask. Great!
Sexy DoodleBob
But this, on the other hand, is maybe the worst thing we saw in the entire store. It was either this or the next thing I’m about to show you. -RV
Sexy Mater
I’m just gonna wrap this up here. -RV

articles.headline: The case for a little election optimism
keyFacts: Democratic voters are casting their ballots in person in large numbers instead of voting by mail this year, according to analysts.
Courts have blocked Trump administration attempts to alter mail voting rules, demand voter rolls, and segregate certain ballots.
Voting groups have prepared lawsuits and public outcry to challenge any attempts by the administration to disrupt the election results.
body: President Donald Trump arrives to speak at a midterm campaign rally in Corpus Christi, Texas on October 27, 2026. | Kent Nishimura/AFP via Getty Images
This story appeared in Today, Explained, a daily newsletter that helps you understand the most compelling news and stories of the day. Subscribe here .
No sooner had early voting started this year than analysts noticed a curious trend: Democratic voters were choosing to vote a lot like…Republicans.

Since the Covid-19 pandemic, Democrats who cast their ballots early have most commonly done so by mail. But this year, they’re voting in person , and in huge numbers — even narrowing Republicans’ traditional early voting lead in states like Florida and Texas.

The abrupt shift may have something to do with President Donald Trump’s attempts to undermine the mail voting process , and it almost definitely reflects the anxiety and vigilance that many Americans feel about the midterms this year. In less than a week, they’ll decide which party controls Congress, along with a slew of state and local offices.

The stakes are arguably unusually high: Voters will choose whether to check the power of a president who has bulldozed over historical norms and limits. So as we count down to that momentous and potentially messy day, I’ve been partnering with my colleague Astead Herndon and Vox’s The Midterms, Actually team for a series of weekly editions on the biggest issues shaping the midterms.

Previously, we dug into the ways both parties are changing , the bipartisan backlash to AI and data centers , the politics of high costs, and the changing mood toward Israel . This week, for our final installment, we’re tackling something a little more fundamental: the integrity and security of the voting process itself. It’s a worrying subject, but by no means a hopeless one. Let’s get into it.
Go a little deeper
Let me begin with a metaphor that may or may not reassure you: Imagine there’s a serial killer outside your house, and they’re trying to get in and kill you.

That’s pretty terrifying, under any circumstance. But also: Your house is an absolute vault . You have reinforced steel doors. You have good locks on all the windows. And the police are actually on its way now.

“I don’t want to understate the threat” of election interference, Benjy Sarlin, Vox’s editorial director of politics said when he relayed this metaphor on the America, Actually podcast last month. But if Trump is the serial killer trying America’s doors and windows…then understand this house is pretty well-defended.

Take mail voting, the issue that has so (literally) moved Democrats this year. You’ll recall that Trump tried to sabotage the practice by implementing new, last-minute rules that would have effectively canceled mail-in voting in some places.

But the Constitution clearly assigns the power to regulate and administer elections to the states and Congress, and courts blocked the administration’s rules. In mid-September, the Supreme Court declined to let them take effect for this election. So there’s one lock made good.

The Trump administration has also demanded unprecedented access to states’ voter rolls, suing 30 states and Washington, DC, to obtain them. Of those cases, courts have dismissed 27 of them (though many dismissals are being appealed).

Earlier this month, the DOJ went further and demanded that California officials set aside the ballots of some 20,000 registered voters that it alleged were likely noncitizens. In the predictable legal battle that followed, courts sided with the state. A federal judge excoriated the administration in an opinion on Wednesday , ruling that the ballot segregation order “would wreak havoc and disrupt the election.” The Trump administration has already appealed the ruling.

Other forms of meddling are possible. Asked in August about declaring a national emergency to impose new voting requirements, Trump replied — unnervingly — that “stranger things have happened.” And the president and his allies have floated drastic measures like deploying federal agents to polling sites or seizing “suspect” ballots, a threat tangible enough that it’s reportedly unsettled a number of FBI agents.

Just last week, the Trump administration attempted to preemptively contest the results in Alaska’s Senate race, claiming that the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot — the incumbent Republican and an independent newcomer — risked confusing voters. The New York Times has since reported that Democrats enticed Dan Sullivan 2.0 to run for exactly that reason. In some corners, the ensuing scandal has raised concerns that Republicans could refuse to seat Democrat Mary Peltola if she wins.

But even that possibility is fairly remote . While there are mechanisms for both state officials and US lawmakers to challenge election results, those procedures are pretty regimented. And any attempts to disrupt voting, vote-counting, or the certification of results would likely face both a flood of lawsuits (which voting groups have already prepped ) and a public outcry that could ultimately and lastingly hurt Republicans.

Trump might not care overmuch about democratic norms or the rule of law, but he does likely care about the risks of a longer-term political backlash. To this day, Benjy said, a lot of Republicans still blame Trump for losing them Georgia’s Senate seats: His election denialism after 2020 helped drive huge numbers of Black Georgians to the polls, where they voted in two Democrats.

The number of Democrats voting early and in-person suggests the possibility that a similar dynamic is at play now. In other words, there is real risk — but lots of people are fighting to keep the proverbial bad guys out.
Races to watch:
Alaska Senate race, where Trump is ready to contest a Democratic win ;
Wisconsin governor’s race, where Republican Tom Tiffany has promoted Trump’s lies about the 2020 election;
Nevada’s secretary of state race, which could similarly put an outspoken election denier in charge of the state’s voting system.

articles.headline: Patrick Stewart, best known for "Star Trek" and "X-Men," dies at 86
keyFacts: Actor Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86 at home on Wednesday following dementia, his spokesperson confirmed.
Stewart was best known for playing Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek, Charles Xavier in X-Men, and award-winning stage roles.
Stewart reprised his role as Charles Xavier in the film Avengers: Doomsday, which will be released in December 2026.
body: Legendary actor Sir Patrick Stewart, best known for his work in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises and his prolific award-winning stage career, has died at 86 years old, his spokesperson confirmed.
Stewart died at home on Wednesday, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said in a statement. His death followed "a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," Novak said.

"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Novak said.
Stewart began his acting career doing stage plays in the United Kingdom, joining the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1960s.

Stewart's most recognizable role began in 1987, when he started playing Enterprise Captain Jean-Luc Picard on "Star Trek: The Next Generation." The show ran for seven seasons and also spawned four "Star Trek" films featuring Stewart as Picard and the rest of the "Next Generation" cast. Stewart later reprised the role for Paramount+ series "Star Trek: Picard," which ran for three seasons.

Fellow "Star Trek" legend William Shatner posted: "Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor. From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work."

Stewart also played X-Men leader Charles Xavier in over half a dozen films in the "X-Men" franchise. He reprised the role for the upcoming "Avengers: Doomsday," which will be released in December 2026. Marvel Studios said on social media that it was "deeply saddened" by Stewart's passing, calling him a "singular talent" who defined the character "for generations of fans."

Stewart appeared in dozens of other film and television roles, including voice work on Seth MacFarlane's animated shows "Family Guy" and "American Dad." But the bulk of his work was on the stage: He was a frequent presence on Broadway and in London's West End, where he played characters from Shakespearean villains to Charles Dickens' Ebenezer Scrooge. He appeared with "X-Men" co-star Ian McKellen in "Waiting for Godot" in London in 2010, then again in New York City in 2013. He also performed his one-man version of "A Christmas Carol" frequently over the decades.

Stewart appeared in over 60 Royal Shakespeare Company productions. The company named him an "Honorary Associate Artist" to celebrate his contributions to their work. He has also been awarded three Olivier Awards for his London stage performances and received one Tony nomination for his work on Broadway.
Stewart was nominated for multiple Emmy, Golden Globe and SAG awards for his on-screen roles. He won a Grammy Award in 1995 for "Best Spoken Word Album for Children."
In 2001, Queen Elizabeth II appointed Stewart an Officer of the Order of the British Empire. In 2010, Stewart received a knighthood, again from Elizabeth II, for his services to drama.
In 2023, Stewart published the memoir "Making It So." The book landed him on the New York Times' best-sellers list. He also recorded a companion audiobook.

Stewart was actively working until 2026. In addition to his role in "Avengers: Doomsday," he recorded an audiobook where he narrated and commented on all 154 of William Shakespeare's sonnets. He also had a voice role in the animated comedy "The Sheep Detectives."

Stewart was married three times. He wed Sheila Falconer in 1966. The pair had two children — Daniel and Sophia — before divorcing in 1990. From 2000 to 2003, he was married to producer Wendy Neuss. In 2008, he began dating singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell. The two married in 2013 and were wed until his death. Novak said Ozell was at Stewart's side when he died.

Stewart was also "a fierce advocate for causes he strongly believed in," his spokesperson said. Those causes included social justice, women's rights, domestic abuse advocacy, veterans' rights, the refugee crisis, animal rights and political reform.

"We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace," Novak said. "His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre. … He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life."
